Component for the /media_classification/api/projects resource.

Retrieve, filter, and export classification project data from Trapper.

Main endpoints:

  • GET /media_classification/api/projects: (listado, paginado y filtrable por query params)
  • GET /media_classification/api/projects/{id}: (detalle de un proyecto de clasificación)
  • `GET /media_classification/api/project/{pk}/collections: collecions en un proyecto de clasificación
  • GET /media_classification/api/collection/{collection_pk}/resources/: recursos clasificados dentro de un project-collection link (collection_pk es el pk devuelto por get_project_collections/find_project_collection, no el pk de la storage collection)

Available filter fields:

|------------------|-------------|-------------| | Parameter | Type | Description | |------------------|-------------|-------------| | owner | boolean | true = projects where user is owner, manager, or has ANY role | status | choice | Filter by project status | research_project | PK | Filter by research project FK | search | str | Searches across: name, owner__username, research_project__name

** Example:: **

for proj in client.classification_projects.all():
    print(proj)

# Export to CSV
client.classification_projects.export(file="/tmp/cs_projects.csv")

class ClassificationProjectsComponent(TrapperComponent[ClassificationProject]):
    """
    Component for the ``/media_classification/api/projects`` resource.

    Retrieve, filter, and export classification project data from Trapper.

    **Main endpoints:**

    - ``GET /media_classification/api/projects``: (listado, paginado y filtrable por query params)
    - ``GET /media_classification/api/projects/{id}``: (detalle de un proyecto de clasificación)
    - ``GET /media_classification/api/project/{pk}/collections`: collecions en un proyecto de clasificación
    - ``GET /media_classification/api/collection/{collection_pk}/resources/``: recursos clasificados
      dentro de un project-collection link (``collection_pk`` es el pk devuelto por
      ``get_project_collections``/``find_project_collection``, no el pk de la storage collection)



    **Available filter fields:**

    |------------------|-------------|-------------|
    | Parameter        | Type        | Description |
    |------------------|-------------|-------------|
    | owner	           | boolean	 | true = projects where user is owner, manager, or has ANY role
    | status	       | choice	     | Filter by project status
    | research_project | PK	         | Filter by research project FK
    | search           | str         | Searches across: name, owner__username, research_project__name


    ** Example:: **

        for proj in client.classification_projects.all():
            print(proj)

        # Export to CSV
        client.classification_projects.export(file="/tmp/cs_projects.csv")
    """

    endpoint = "/media_classification/api/projects"
    schema = ClassificationProject
    endpoint_collections="/media_classification/api/project/{project_pk}/collections"

    def _collections_entrypoint(self, pk: int):
        return self.endpoint_collections.format(project_pk=pk)

    def get_project_collections(
        self,
        project_pk: int,
        query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        page: int = 1,
        page_size: int = 50,
        validate: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> PaginatedResult[ClassificationProjectCollection]:
        """Fetch one page of collections linked to a classification project.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            query: Base query parameters.
            page: Page number to fetch.
            page_size: Number of items per page.
            validate: Whether to validate each row with Pydantic.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            Paginated result containing ``ClassificationProjectCollection`` items.
        """

        return self.get(
            query=query,
            page=page,
            page_size=page_size,
            validate=validate,
            overwrite_endpoint=self._collections_entrypoint(project_pk),
            overwrite_schema=ClassificationProjectCollection,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def where_project_collections(
        self,
        project_pk: int,
        query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        page_size: int = 50,
        validate: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> APIQuery[ClassificationProjectCollection]:
        """Return a lazy iterator over collections linked to a project.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            query: Base query parameters.
            page_size: Number of items requested per API page.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            Lazy ``APIQuery`` iterator yielding project collections.
        """
        return self.where(
            query=query,
            page_size=page_size,
            overwrite_endpoint=self._collections_entrypoint(project_pk),
            overwrite_schema=ClassificationProjectCollection,
            validate=validate,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def find_project_collection(
        self,
        project_pk: int,
        pk: int | str,
        query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        validate: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> ClassificationProjectCollection:
        """Retrieve one project-collection link by primary key.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            pk: Project-collection link primary key. NOT collection pk
        Returns:
            ``ClassificationProjectCollection``
        """
        return self.find(
            pk=pk,
            overwrite_endpoint=self._collections_entrypoint(project_pk),
            overwrite_schema=ClassificationProjectCollection,
            validate=validate,
            query=query,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def get_all_project_collections(
        self,
        project_pk: int,
        query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        page_size: int = 50,
        validate: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> PaginatedResult[ClassificationProjectCollection]:
        """Fetch all pages of collections linked to a classification project.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            query: Base query parameters.
            page_size: Number of items requested per API page.
            validate: Whether to validate each row with Pydantic.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            Paginated result containing merged ``ClassificationProjectCollection`` items.
        """
        return self.get_all(
            query=query,
            page_size=page_size,
            validate=validate,
            overwrite_endpoint=self._collections_entrypoint(project_pk),
            overwrite_schema=ClassificationProjectCollection,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def find_collection_in_project(
            self,
            project_pk: int,
            collection_pk: int,
            **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> int | None:
        """Check whether a collection is linked to a classification project.

        Iterates the project-collection links lazily and returns the pk of the
        link record if found, or ``None`` if the collection is not linked to
        the project.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            collection_pk: Collection primary key to search for.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters passed to the underlying request.

        Returns:
            The pk of the project-collection link if found, otherwise ``None``.

        Example::

            link_pk = client.classificacion_projects.find_collection_in_project(
                project_pk=7,
                collection_pk=42,
            )
            if link_pk:
                print(f"Collection 42 is linked via pk={link_pk}")
            else:
                print("Collection 42 is not in this project")
        """
        for link in self.where_project_collections(project_pk=project_pk, **kwargs):
            if link.collection_pk == collection_pk:
                return link.pk
        return None

    # ── write access (Trapper v1: the classic web forms) ──────────────────────

    create_endpoint = "media_classification/project/create/"
    add_collections_endpoint = "media_classification/project/collection/add/"
    remove_collection_endpoint = "media_classification/project/collection/delete/{link_pk}/"
    _ROLES_PREFIX = "classification_project_roles"

    def create(
        self,
        project: ClassificationProjectCreate,
        *,
        raise_on_error: bool = True,
    ) -> ClassificationProject | None:
        """Create a classification project (**Trapper v1 only**).

        The REST API is read-only for classification projects, so this simulates the classic web
        form ``media_classification/project/create/`` with cookie/session authentication, as
        :meth:`~trapper_client.components.research_projects.ResearchProjectsComponent.create` does.
        The account that logs in becomes the owner and administrator. The project is empty: link
        its collections with :meth:`add_collections`.

        Warning:
            It depends on an unversioned HTML form, and needs ``user_name``/``user_password`` (the
            *email* on servers that log in by email): a token alone cannot authenticate it.

        Args:
            project: A :class:`~trapper_client.schemas.classifications.ClassificationProjectCreate`,
                which validates it before anything is sent. The research project must be one the
                account can edit.
            raise_on_error: Raise ``APIError`` when the server rejects the form (the default);
                with ``False`` return ``None`` instead.

        Returns:
            The created project, or ``None`` when it cannot be read back (or the server rejected
            the form and ``raise_on_error=False``).

        Raises:
            TypeError: ``project`` is not a ``ClassificationProjectCreate``.
            err.UnsupportedVersionError: On Trapper v2.
            err.APIError: The server rejected the form (an unknown research project or classificator,
                no permission, ...) or redirected to its login page.

        Example::

            project = client.classification_projects.create(
                ClassificationProjectCreate(name="Doñana 2026", research_project=3, classificator=2)
            )
        """
        self._require_version("v1", feature="classification_projects.create()")
        if not isinstance(project, ClassificationProjectCreate):
            raise TypeError(
                f"create() takes a ClassificationProjectCreate, not {type(project).__name__}; "
                "build one with ClassificationProjectCreate(...) or "
                "ClassificationProjectCreate.model_validate(data)"
            )

        known = {p.pk for p in self.where(search=project.name, page_size=50) if p.name == project.name}
        data = project.to_form()
        data.update(
            self._owner_role_fields(
                self.create_endpoint, self._ROLES_PREFIX, "classification project", project.role_rows()
            )
        )
        if self._submit_create_form(self.create_endpoint, data, "Classification project", raise_on_error) is None:
            return None
        created = [
            p for p in self.where(search=project.name, page_size=50)
            if p.name == project.name and p.pk not in known
        ]
        return max(created, key=lambda p: p.pk, default=None)

    def add_collections(
        self,
        project_pk: int,
        collection_pks: Iterable[int],
    ) -> list[ClassificationProjectCollection]:
        """Link storage collections to a classification project (**Trapper v1 only**).

        Simulates the web action ``media_classification/project/collection/add/``. Trapper only
        takes collections that are already part of the project's *research project*, and where the
        account administers it; linking a collection to a research project is a web action the SDK
        does not cover. A collection that is already in the project is left as it is.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            collection_pks: Primary keys of the *storage collections* (``Collection.pk``), not of
                the research-project or project links.

        Returns:
            The project's links for those collections.

        Raises:
            ValueError: A collection is not in the project's research project.
            err.UnsupportedVersionError: On Trapper v2.
            err.APIError: Trapper refused the action, or it left a collection unlinked.
        """
        self._require_version("v1", feature="classification_projects.add_collections()")
        wanted = list(dict.fromkeys(int(pk) for pk in collection_pks))
        if not wanted:
            raise ValueError("collection_pks is empty")

        def links():
            return {l.collection_pk: l for l in self.where_project_collections(project_pk=project_pk)}

        present = links()
        missing = [pk for pk in wanted if pk not in present]
        if missing:
            project = self.find(project_pk)
            research_pk = self._research_project_pk(project.research_project)
            research_links = {
                l.collection_pk: l.pk
                for l in self.client.research_projects.where_project_collections(project_pk=research_pk)
            }
            unknown = [pk for pk in missing if pk not in research_links]
            if unknown:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"collections {unknown} are not in the research project '{project.research_project}' "
                    f"(pk {research_pk}); a classification project can only use the collections of its "
                    "research project"
                )
            response = self.client.session_post_multipart(
                self.add_collections_endpoint,
                data={
                    "project": project_pk,
                    "rproject": research_pk,
                    "collections_pks": ",".join(str(research_links[pk]) for pk in missing),
                },
            )
            self._check_json_action(response, "Adding collections to the classification project")
            present = links()
            still = [pk for pk in missing if pk not in present]
            if still:
                raise err.APIError(f"Trapper accepted the request but collections {still} are still not linked")
        return [present[pk] for pk in wanted]

    def remove_collection(self, project_pk: int, collection_pk: int) -> bool:
        """Unlink a collection from a classification project (**Trapper v1 only**).

        Simulates the web action ``media_classification/project/collection/delete/<pk>/``.

        Warning:
            It is irreversible, and the classifications made on that collection **in this project
            are deleted with the link** (the database cascades). The collection and its resources
            are not touched.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            collection_pk: Primary key of the *storage collection* to unlink.

        Returns:
            ``True`` once the collection is no longer linked; ``False`` if it never was.

        Raises:
            err.UnsupportedVersionError: On Trapper v2.
            err.APIError: Trapper did not remove it (typically: no permission to edit the project).
        """
        self._require_version("v1", feature="classification_projects.remove_collection()")
        link_pk = self.find_collection_in_project(project_pk=project_pk, collection_pk=collection_pk)
        if link_pk is None:
            return False
        self.client.session_login()
        url = f"{self.client.base_url.rstrip('/')}/{self.remove_collection_endpoint.format(link_pk=link_pk)}"
        self.client._web_client.get(url)
        if self.find_collection_in_project(project_pk=project_pk, collection_pk=collection_pk) is not None:
            raise err.APIError(
                f"Trapper did not unlink collection {collection_pk} from project {project_pk}: "
                "the account may not be allowed to edit the project"
            )
        return True

    def _research_project_pk(self, name: str) -> int:
        """Primary key of a research project from its name (the project API gives only the name).

        Names are unique in Trapper, so an exact match identifies it.
        """
        matches = [p for p in self.client.research_projects.where(search=name, page_size=50) if p.name == name]
        if len(matches) != 1:
            raise err.APIError(f"Cannot tell which research project '{name}' is ({len(matches)} matches)")
        return matches[0].pk

    @staticmethod
    def _check_json_action(response: Any, label: str) -> None:
        """Raise unless a JSON web action (``{"success": ..., "msg": ...}``) succeeded."""
        try:
            body = response.json()
        except ValueError:
            raise err.APIError(f"{label} failed (status {response.status_code}): the answer is not JSON")
        if not body.get("success"):
            raise err.APIError(f"{label} failed: {body.get('msg') or 'no reason given'}")

    # ── classification resources sub-endpoint ────────────────────────────────

    endpoint_resources = "media_classification/api/collection/{collection_pk}/resources/"

    def _resources_entrypoint(self, collection_pk: int) -> str:
        return self.endpoint_resources.format(collection_pk=collection_pk)

    def get_collection_resources(
        self,
        collection_pk: int,
        query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        page: int = 1,
        page_size: int = 50,
        validate: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> PaginatedResult[ClassifiedResource]:
        """Fetch one page of classified resources within a project-collection link.

        Args:
            collection_pk: Project-collection link primary key (see
                :meth:`get_project_collections`/:meth:`find_project_collection`).
            query: Base query parameters (accepts ``ClassificationFilter`` fields).
            page: Page number to fetch.
            page_size: Number of items per page.
            validate: Whether to validate each row with Pydantic.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            ``PaginatedResult[ClassifiedResource]`` for the requested page.
        """
        return self.get(
            query=query,
            page=page,
            page_size=page_size,
            validate=validate,
            overwrite_endpoint=self._resources_entrypoint(collection_pk),
            overwrite_schema=ClassifiedResource,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def where_collection_resources(
        self,
        collection_pk: int,
        query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        page_size: int = 50,
        validate: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> APIQuery[ClassifiedResource]:
        """Return a lazy iterator over classified resources within a project-collection link.

        Args:
            collection_pk: Project-collection link primary key.
            query: Base query parameters (accepts ``ClassificationFilter`` fields).
            page_size: Number of items requested per API page.
            validate: Whether to validate each row with Pydantic.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            Lazy ``APIQuery[ClassifiedResource]`` iterator.
        """
        return self.where(
            query=query,
            page_size=page_size,
            validate=validate,
            overwrite_endpoint=self._resources_entrypoint(collection_pk),
            overwrite_schema=ClassifiedResource,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def get_all_collection_resources(
        self,
        collection_pk: int,
        query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        page_size: int = 50,
        validate: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> PaginatedResult[ClassifiedResource]:
        """Fetch all pages of classified resources within a project-collection link.

        Args:
            collection_pk: Project-collection link primary key.
            query: Base query parameters (accepts ``ClassificationFilter`` fields).
            page_size: Number of items per page requested from the API.
            validate: Whether to validate each row with Pydantic.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            ``PaginatedResult[ClassifiedResource]`` with all items merged.
        """
        return self.get_all(
            query=query,
            page_size=page_size,
            validate=validate,
            overwrite_endpoint=self._resources_entrypoint(collection_pk),
            overwrite_schema=ClassifiedResource,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def get_collection_resources_around(
        self,
        collection_pk: int,
        resource_pk: int,
        size: int = 5,
        query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        validate: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> PaginatedResult[ClassifiedResource]:
        """Fetch resources surrounding one resource within a project-collection link.

        Uses the server's windowed pagination (``current``/``size`` query
        params) instead of page-based pagination: returns up to ``size``
        resources on each side of ``resource_pk`` (ordered by
        ``date_recorded``), which is how the classification UI implements
        "previous/next" navigation. The response's ``pagination`` block
        carries ``total``/``filtered`` counts instead of the usual
        ``page``/``pages``/``count`` fields.

        Args:
            collection_pk: Project-collection link primary key.
            resource_pk: Resource primary key to center the window on.
            size: Number of resources to fetch on each side of ``resource_pk``.
            query: Base query parameters (accepts ``ClassificationFilter`` fields).
            validate: Whether to validate each row with Pydantic.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            ``PaginatedResult[ClassifiedResource]`` with
            ``pagination.total`` and ``pagination.filtered`` populated.

        Example::

            page = client.classification_projects.get_collection_resources_around(
                collection_pk=12, resource_pk=4831, size=5,
            )
            print(page.pagination.total, page.pagination.filtered)
        """
        q = self._merge_query(query, kwargs)
        q["current"] = resource_pk
        q["size"] = size
        data = self.client.get(self._resources_entrypoint(collection_pk), query=q)
        return self._to_paginated(data, validate=validate, schema=ClassifiedResource)

def create(
    self,
    project: ClassificationProjectCreate,
    *,
    raise_on_error: bool = True,
) -> ClassificationProject | None:
    """Create a classification project (**Trapper v1 only**).

    The REST API is read-only for classification projects, so this simulates the classic web
    form ``media_classification/project/create/`` with cookie/session authentication, as
    :meth:`~trapper_client.components.research_projects.ResearchProjectsComponent.create` does.
    The account that logs in becomes the owner and administrator. The project is empty: link
    its collections with :meth:`add_collections`.

    Warning:
        It depends on an unversioned HTML form, and needs ``user_name``/``user_password`` (the
        *email* on servers that log in by email): a token alone cannot authenticate it.

    Args:
        project: A :class:`~trapper_client.schemas.classifications.ClassificationProjectCreate`,
            which validates it before anything is sent. The research project must be one the
            account can edit.
        raise_on_error: Raise ``APIError`` when the server rejects the form (the default);
            with ``False`` return ``None`` instead.

    Returns:
        The created project, or ``None`` when it cannot be read back (or the server rejected
        the form and ``raise_on_error=False``).

    Raises:
        TypeError: ``project`` is not a ``ClassificationProjectCreate``.
        err.UnsupportedVersionError: On Trapper v2.
        err.APIError: The server rejected the form (an unknown research project or classificator,
            no permission, ...) or redirected to its login page.

    Example::

        project = client.classification_projects.create(
            ClassificationProjectCreate(name="Doñana 2026", research_project=3, classificator=2)
        )
    """
    self._require_version("v1", feature="classification_projects.create()")
    if not isinstance(project, ClassificationProjectCreate):
        raise TypeError(
            f"create() takes a ClassificationProjectCreate, not {type(project).__name__}; "
            "build one with ClassificationProjectCreate(...) or "
            "ClassificationProjectCreate.model_validate(data)"
        )

    known = {p.pk for p in self.where(search=project.name, page_size=50) if p.name == project.name}
    data = project.to_form()
    data.update(
        self._owner_role_fields(
            self.create_endpoint, self._ROLES_PREFIX, "classification project", project.role_rows()
        )
    )
    if self._submit_create_form(self.create_endpoint, data, "Classification project", raise_on_error) is None:
        return None
    created = [
        p for p in self.where(search=project.name, page_size=50)
        if p.name == project.name and p.pk not in known
    ]
    return max(created, key=lambda p: p.pk, default=None)

def add_collections(
    self,
    project_pk: int,
    collection_pks: Iterable[int],
) -> list[ClassificationProjectCollection]:
    """Link storage collections to a classification project (**Trapper v1 only**).

    Simulates the web action ``media_classification/project/collection/add/``. Trapper only
    takes collections that are already part of the project's *research project*, and where the
    account administers it; linking a collection to a research project is a web action the SDK
    does not cover. A collection that is already in the project is left as it is.

    Args:
        project_pk: Classification project primary key.
        collection_pks: Primary keys of the *storage collections* (``Collection.pk``), not of
            the research-project or project links.

    Returns:
        The project's links for those collections.

    Raises:
        ValueError: A collection is not in the project's research project.
        err.UnsupportedVersionError: On Trapper v2.
        err.APIError: Trapper refused the action, or it left a collection unlinked.
    """
    self._require_version("v1", feature="classification_projects.add_collections()")
    wanted = list(dict.fromkeys(int(pk) for pk in collection_pks))
    if not wanted:
        raise ValueError("collection_pks is empty")

    def links():
        return {l.collection_pk: l for l in self.where_project_collections(project_pk=project_pk)}

    present = links()
    missing = [pk for pk in wanted if pk not in present]
    if missing:
        project = self.find(project_pk)
        research_pk = self._research_project_pk(project.research_project)
        research_links = {
            l.collection_pk: l.pk
            for l in self.client.research_projects.where_project_collections(project_pk=research_pk)
        }
        unknown = [pk for pk in missing if pk not in research_links]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"collections {unknown} are not in the research project '{project.research_project}' "
                f"(pk {research_pk}); a classification project can only use the collections of its "
                "research project"
            )
        response = self.client.session_post_multipart(
            self.add_collections_endpoint,
            data={
                "project": project_pk,
                "rproject": research_pk,
                "collections_pks": ",".join(str(research_links[pk]) for pk in missing),
            },
        )
        self._check_json_action(response, "Adding collections to the classification project")
        present = links()
        still = [pk for pk in missing if pk not in present]
        if still:
            raise err.APIError(f"Trapper accepted the request but collections {still} are still not linked")
    return [present[pk] for pk in wanted]

def remove_collection(self, project_pk: int, collection_pk: int) -> bool:
    """Unlink a collection from a classification project (**Trapper v1 only**).

    Simulates the web action ``media_classification/project/collection/delete/<pk>/``.

    Warning:
        It is irreversible, and the classifications made on that collection **in this project
        are deleted with the link** (the database cascades). The collection and its resources
        are not touched.

    Args:
        project_pk: Classification project primary key.
        collection_pk: Primary key of the *storage collection* to unlink.

    Returns:
        ``True`` once the collection is no longer linked; ``False`` if it never was.

    Raises:
        err.UnsupportedVersionError: On Trapper v2.
        err.APIError: Trapper did not remove it (typically: no permission to edit the project).
    """
    self._require_version("v1", feature="classification_projects.remove_collection()")
    link_pk = self.find_collection_in_project(project_pk=project_pk, collection_pk=collection_pk)
    if link_pk is None:
        return False
    self.client.session_login()
    url = f"{self.client.base_url.rstrip('/')}/{self.remove_collection_endpoint.format(link_pk=link_pk)}"
    self.client._web_client.get(url)
    if self.find_collection_in_project(project_pk=project_pk, collection_pk=collection_pk) is not None:
        raise err.APIError(
            f"Trapper did not unlink collection {collection_pk} from project {project_pk}: "
            "the account may not be allowed to edit the project"
        )
    return True

def get_collection_resources_around(
    self,
    collection_pk: int,
    resource_pk: int,
    size: int = 5,
    query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    validate: bool = True,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> PaginatedResult[ClassifiedResource]:
    """Fetch resources surrounding one resource within a project-collection link.

    Uses the server's windowed pagination (``current``/``size`` query
    params) instead of page-based pagination: returns up to ``size``
    resources on each side of ``resource_pk`` (ordered by
    ``date_recorded``), which is how the classification UI implements
    "previous/next" navigation. The response's ``pagination`` block
    carries ``total``/``filtered`` counts instead of the usual
    ``page``/``pages``/``count`` fields.

    Args:
        collection_pk: Project-collection link primary key.
        resource_pk: Resource primary key to center the window on.
        size: Number of resources to fetch on each side of ``resource_pk``.
        query: Base query parameters (accepts ``ClassificationFilter`` fields).
        validate: Whether to validate each row with Pydantic.
        **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

    Returns:
        ``PaginatedResult[ClassifiedResource]`` with
        ``pagination.total`` and ``pagination.filtered`` populated.

    Example::

        page = client.classification_projects.get_collection_resources_around(
            collection_pk=12, resource_pk=4831, size=5,
        )
        print(page.pagination.total, page.pagination.filtered)
    """
    q = self._merge_query(query, kwargs)
    q["current"] = resource_pk
    q["size"] = size
    data = self.client.get(self._resources_entrypoint(collection_pk), query=q)

class ClassificationResultsAggComponent(TrapperComponent[ClassificationAgg]):
    """
    Component for ``/media_classification/api/classifications/results/agg/{project_pk}/``.

    Available endpoints:
    - ``GET /media_classification/api/classifications/results/agg/{project_pk}/``

    This endpoint returns CSV (gzip) by default, or GeoJSON when ``geojson=True``.
    """

    endpoint = "media_classification/api/classifications/results/agg/{project_pk}/"
    schema = ClassificationAgg

    def get_project_results_agg(
        self,
        project_pk: int,
        query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        page: int = 1,
        page_size: int = 50,
        validate: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> PaginatedResult[ClassificationAgg]:
        """Fetch one page of aggregated results for a project.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            query: Base query parameters.
            page: Page number to fetch.
            page_size: Number of items per page.
            validate: Whether to validate each row with Pydantic.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            Paginated result containing ``ClassificationAgg`` items.
        """
        q = self._merge_query(query, kwargs)
        q = dict(q or {})
        q.setdefault("page", page)
        q.setdefault("page_size", page_size)

        endpoint = self.endpoint.replace("{project_pk}", str(project_pk))
        data = self.client.get(endpoint, query=q)
        return self._to_paginated(data, validate=validate)

    def export_project_results_agg(
        self,
        project_pk: int,
        query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        file: str | Path | None = None,
        validate: bool = True,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> Path:
        """Export aggregated results of one project to CSV.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            query: Base query parameters.
            file: Output CSV file path. If ``None``, a temp file is created.
            validate: If ``True``, validates rows before writing CSV.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            Path to the generated CSV file.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``geojson=True`` is requested, because this method only
                supports CSV export.
        """
        q = self._merge_query(query, kwargs)
        q = dict(q or {})
        if str(q.get("geojson", "False")).lower() == "true":
            raise ValueError("export_project_results_agg only supports CSV export; use get_project_results_agg with geojson=True")

        endpoint = self.endpoint.replace("{project_pk}", str(project_pk))

        if not validate:
            return self.client.export_all(endpoint, query=q, file=file)

        data = self.client.get_all(endpoint, query=q)
        parsed = self._to_paginated(data, validate=True)
        output_path = self.client._select_file(file)
        rows = [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in parsed.results]
        self.client._write_csv(rows, output_path)
        return output_path

class ClassificationsComponent(ClassificationFiltersMixin, TrapperComponent[Classification]):
    """
    The **final classifications** of a classification project (``client.classification_results``).

    In a classification project every resource has one final classification: the record that holds its result,
    taken from the classification someone made or imported and then approved. It is a set of observations
    (zero, one or several). It is read in three ways, each with its own shape:

    - ``GET /media_classification/api/classifications`` (and ``/{pk}``): the **list**, one row per resource.
      Its ``dynamic_attrs`` only have the observation type, the species (as text) and the count.
    - ``GET /media_classification/api/classifications/results/{project_pk}/``: the **results table**, a gzip CSV with
      one row per observation (``get_project_results``, ``where_project_results``, ``export_project_results``).
      Use it to know what each image shows. ``camtrapdp=False`` is the format with ``_id``, the one that can be imported.
    - ``POST /media_classification/api/classifications/import/``: **import** observations from a CSV, by ``_id``
      (``import_classifications``). It updates final classifications that exist; it does not create them.

    The API cannot create, edit or approve a classification otherwise. Not to be confused with
    ``client.classification_media`` (the table of the project's files) or the user and AI classification lists.
    See the classifications guide for the details, including boxes and what ``_id`` and ``observationID`` are.

    **Filters** of the list and the results table (Trapper ignores any other without an error; the SDK emits an
    ``UnknownFilterWarning``):

    | Parameter | Type | Description |
    |---|---|---|
    | project | PK | The project of the list. **Needed for deployment and collection** (``ValueError`` without it) |
    | owner | boolean | true = resources where the user is owner/manager |
    | deployment | list of PKs | Deployment PKs of the project |
    | collection | list of PKs | PK of the **link** between the project and the collection, not the collection's PK |
    | locations_map | comma-separated PKs | Location PKs |
    | rdate_from / rdate_to | date | ``date_recorded`` range |
    | rtime_from / rtime_to | HH:MM | Time-of-day range |
    | ftype | choice | Resource type (IMAGE, VIDEO, ...) |
    | classified / classified_ai | boolean | Has a classification by a user / by AI (``500`` on v2 in the results table) |
    | approved | boolean | Approved. Works on both versions: v1 calls it ``status`` and the SDK sends it as such |
    | bboxes | boolean | Has bounding boxes |
    | species | list of PKs | Species PKs |
    | observation_type, sex, age | choice | Observation type, sex, age |

    ``user``, ``feedback``, ``confidence`` and ``ai_provider`` are filters of the user and AI classification lists:
    they do nothing here.

    **Extra parameter of the results table:**

    | Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | camtrapdp | boolean | ``True`` | ``True`` = Camtrap DP rows, ``False`` = Trapper's own format (with ``_id``) |
    """

    #: ``camtrapdp`` is a parameter of the results table, not a filter.
    known_filters = ClassificationFiltersMixin._filters_for(frozenset({"camtrapdp"}))

    endpoint = "/media_classification/api/classifications"
    export_endpoint = "/media_classification/api/classifications/results/{project_pk}/"
    schema = Classification
    export_schema = ClassificationRecordExport

    # ── the list needs a project for deployment and collection ────────────────

    def _require_project(self, query: Dict[str, Any] | None, kwargs: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """``deployment`` and ``collection`` of the list are checked by Trapper against the project's own.

        Without ``project`` it answers ``400 "Select a valid choice. 19 is not one of the available choices"``,
        which reads as if the deployment did not exist. The project-scoped methods (``overwrite_endpoint``) have it
        in the URL and need nothing.
        """
        if kwargs.get("overwrite_endpoint"):
            return
        given = {**(query or {}), **kwargs}
        needing = [name for name in ("deployment", "collection") if name in given]
        if needing and "project" not in given:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{' and '.join(needing)} of the classification list need project=<pk>: Trapper checks them against "
                "the project's own and otherwise answers 400 'Select a valid choice'. Add project, or use "
                "where_project_results() (the project is in its URL)."
            )

    def get(self, query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any):
        """One page of the list; see :meth:`TrapperComponent.get`. ``deployment`` and ``collection`` need ``project``."""
        self._require_project(query, kwargs)
        return super().get(query, *args, **kwargs)

    def where(self, query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any):
        """Lazy iteration; see :meth:`TrapperComponent.where`. ``deployment`` and ``collection`` need ``project``."""
        self._require_project(query, kwargs)
        return super().where(query, *args, **kwargs)

    def get_all(self, query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any):
        """Every page; see :meth:`TrapperComponent.get_all`. ``deployment`` and ``collection`` need ``project``."""
        self._require_project(query, kwargs)
        return super().get_all(query, *args, **kwargs)

    def _resolve_export_endpoint(self, project_pk: int) -> str:
        """Build the export endpoint for a given project pk."""
        return self.export_endpoint.format(project_pk=project_pk)

    def get_project_results(
            self,
            project_pk: int,
            query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
            page: int = 1,
            page_size: int = 50,
            validate: bool = True,
            **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> PaginatedResult[ClassificationRecordExport]:
        """Fetch one page of observation rows for a classification project.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            query: Base query parameters.
            page: Page number to fetch.
            page_size: Number of items per page.
            validate: Whether to validate each row with Pydantic.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            Paginated result containing ``ClassificationResultRecord`` items.
        """
        return self.get(
            query=query,
            page=page,
            page_size=page_size,
            validate=validate,
            overwrite_endpoint=self._resolve_export_endpoint(project_pk),
            overwrite_schema=self.export_schema,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def where_project_results(
            self,
            project_pk: int,
            query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
            page_size: int = 50,
            validate: bool = True,
            **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> APIQuery[ClassificationRecordExport]:
        """Return a lazy iterator over observation rows for a project.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            query: Base query parameters.
            page_size: Number of items requested per API page.
            validate: Whether to validate each row with Pydantic.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            Lazy ``APIQuery[ClassificationResultRecord]`` iterator.
        """
        return self.where(
            query=query,
            page_size=page_size,
            validate=validate,
            overwrite_endpoint=self._resolve_export_endpoint(project_pk),
            overwrite_schema=self.export_schema,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def export_project_results(
            self,
            project_pk: int,
            query: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
            file: str | Path | None = None,
            validate: bool = True,
            **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> Path | list[ClassificationRecordExport]:
        """Export observation rows for one project to CSV or model list.

        Args:
            project_pk: Classification project primary key.
            query: Base query parameters.
            file: Output CSV file path. If ``None``, returns a list of models.
            validate: Whether to validate rows with Pydantic.
            **kwargs: Extra query parameters merged into ``query``.

        Returns:
            ``Path`` when ``file`` is provided, otherwise ``list[BaseModel]``.
        """
        return self.export(
            query=query,
            file=file,
            validate=validate,
            overwrite_endpoint=self._resolve_export_endpoint(project_pk),
            **kwargs,
        )

    def import_classifications(
            self,
            project_id: int,
            file: str | Path,
            approve: bool = True,
            import_bboxes: bool = True,
            import_expert_classifications: bool = True,
            import_ai_classifications: bool = False,
            overwrite_attrs: bool = False,
            ai_provider_id: int | str | None = None,
            validate: bool = True,
            check_table: bool = True,
            split: bool = False,
            delay: float = 1.0,
            chunk_size: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES,
            retry_attempts: int = 3,
            retry_min_wait: float = 1.0,
            retry_max_wait: float = 10.0,
            raise_on_error: bool = True,
    ) -> Union[
        ClassificationImportResponse, Dict[str, Any],
        List[Union[ClassificationImportResponse, Dict[str, Any]]],
    ]:
        """Import expert/AI observations from a CSV file into a classification project.

        Posts to ``media_classification/api/classifications/import/``. The CSV
        must follow the internal Trapper format and contain an ``_id`` column.
        Depending on server configuration the import runs synchronously or is
        scheduled as a Celery task, in which case the response carries a
        ``task_id`` instead of a final result message.

        Args:
            project_id: Classification project primary key.
            file: Path to the observations CSV file to upload.
            approve: Mark imported classifications as approved.
            import_bboxes: Import bounding boxes present in the ``bboxes`` column.
            import_expert_classifications: Import rows with classificationMethod = human.
            import_ai_classifications: Import rows with classificationMethod = machine.
                Requires ``ai_provider_id``.
            overwrite_attrs: Overwrite existing classification attributes when
                approving imported AI classifications. **Trapper v1 only**: v2 removed
                the option, so ``True`` raises ``UnsupportedVersionError`` there.
            ai_provider_id: AI provider primary key. Required when
                ``import_ai_classifications=True``.
            check_table: Check the table locally first (required columns, ``sex`` values) and
                raise ``ValueError`` instead of sending a table Trapper would reject with a bare 500.
            validate: Whether to validate the response with Pydantic.
            split: Instead of uploading ``file`` in one request, split it into
                several smaller, self-contained CSV chunks (each repeating the
                header row) and import them one request at a time, sleeping
                ``delay`` seconds between uploads. Unlike
                :meth:`~trapper_client.components.locations.LocationsComponent.import_locations`,
                this endpoint is a real REST API that can usually take a full
                file in one request — this is only useful as a workaround for
                very large CSVs that hit request-size limits (this server's
                ``DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE``/reverse-proxy limits) or time
                out. There is no real chunked/resumable upload protocol here
                (see :mod:`trapper_client.csv_chunking`).
            delay: Seconds to sleep between chunk uploads when ``split=True``.
                Ignored otherwise.
            chunk_size: Maximum size in bytes of each chunk when ``split=True``.
                Ignored otherwise. Defaults to 512 KiB.
            retry_attempts: Maximum number of attempts (first try + retries)
                per chunk/file upload when the request fails with a
                network-level error (read timeout, connection reset, ...) —
                the failure mode expected when a chunk is still too large or
                slow for the server. Does not retry on HTTP error responses
                (those are validation failures a retry can't fix). Set to
                ``1`` to disable retrying.
            retry_min_wait: Minimum exponential backoff delay in seconds
                between retry attempts.
            retry_max_wait: Maximum exponential backoff delay in seconds
                between retry attempts.
            raise_on_error: Whether to raise mapped API exceptions (e.g. missing
                project/AI provider, or invalid CSV rows returned as a 400).
                With ``split=True``, raises as soon as one chunk fails rather
                than uploading the rest.

        Returns:
            ``ClassificationImportResponse`` when ``validate=True``, otherwise
            the raw response dict. When ``split=True``, a list with one such
            result per chunk (in file order) instead of a single result.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``import_ai_classifications=True`` but ``ai_provider_id`` is not set.
            err.APIError: If the import fails (a 4xx/5xx response) and
                ``raise_on_error=True``. The exception message includes the
                server's actual ``data.message``/``data.errors`` (e.g. Django
                form errors per field) when the response is JSON — but a
                genuine unhandled server-side exception (as opposed to a
                validation failure) returns Django's plain HTML error page
                instead, with no JSON body at all; this method detects that
                case and raises a clear error with a text snippet rather than
                crashing on ``response.json()``.

        Example::

            result = client.classification_results.import_classifications(
                project_id=7, file="/tmp/observations.csv",
            )
            print(result.data.message, result.data.task_id)

            # A very large CSV, uploaded in <=512 KiB chunks, 2s apart:
            results = client.classification_results.import_classifications(
                project_id=7, file="/tmp/huge_observations.csv",
                split=True, delay=2,
            )
        """
        if import_ai_classifications and ai_provider_id is None:
            raise ValueError("ai_provider_id is required when import_ai_classifications=True")
        if check_table:
            self._check_table(Path(file))
        if overwrite_attrs:
            # Trapper v2's import view no longer reads it, so it would be dropped silently.
            self._require_version("v1", feature="classification_results.import_classifications(overwrite_attrs=True)")

        data: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "project_id": project_id,
            "approve": approve,
            "import_bboxes": import_bboxes,
            "import_expert_classifications": import_expert_classifications,
        }
        if overwrite_attrs:
            data["overwrite_attrs"] = True
        if import_ai_classifications:
            # Sent only when True: the server reads this flag from the raw
            # request body *before* running it through form validation, as a
            # plain Python truthy check — a literal "False" string sent over
            # multipart would still be truthy there.
            data["import_ai_classifications"] = True
            data["ai_provider_id"] = ai_provider_id

        retrying = retrying_for_chunk_upload(retry_attempts, retry_min_wait, retry_max_wait)

        if not split:
            return self._import_classifications_once(data, Path(file), validate, raise_on_error, retrying)

        chunk_paths = split_csv_by_size(file, max_bytes=chunk_size)
        try:
            results = []
            for i, chunk_path in enumerate(chunk_paths):
                results.append(
                    self._import_classifications_once(data, chunk_path, validate, raise_on_error, retrying)
                )
                if i < len(chunk_paths) - 1:
                    time.sleep(delay)
            return results
        finally:
            for chunk_path in chunk_paths:
                chunk_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    #: Values Trapper accepts for ``sex`` (anything else fails validation).
    VALID_SEX = ("female", "male")
    #: Columns Trapper's importer cannot do without.
    REQUIRED_COLUMNS = ("_id", "classificationMethod")

    @classmethod
    def _check_table(cls, file_path: Path) -> None:
        """Catch locally what Trapper would answer with a bare HTTP 500.

        Checks the required columns and the ``sex`` enum. Raises ``ValueError``
        listing every problem found (first 10 rows for the enum).
        """
        with file_path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
            reader = csv.DictReader(fh)
            header = reader.fieldnames or []
            problems = [f"missing column '{c}'" for c in cls.REQUIRED_COLUMNS if c not in header]
            if "sex" in header:
                bad = [
                    f"row {n}: sex={row['sex']!r}"
                    for n, row in enumerate(reader, start=2)
                    if (row.get("sex") or "").strip() and row["sex"].strip() not in cls.VALID_SEX
                ]
                if bad:
                    problems.append(f"sex must be one of {cls.VALID_SEX} ({'; '.join(bad[:10])})")
        if problems:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{file_path.name} would be rejected by Trapper: " + "; ".join(problems)
                + ". Pass check_table=False to skip this check."
            )

    def _import_classifications_once(
            self,
            data: Dict[str, Any],
            file_path: Path,
            validate: bool,
            raise_on_error: bool,
            retrying: Retrying,
    ) -> ClassificationImportResponse | Dict[str, Any]:
        """Perform one ``media_classification/api/classifications/import/`` POST for a single CSV file."""
        endpoint = f"{self.endpoint.rstrip('/')}/import/"
        with file_path.open("rb") as fh:
            def _do_request():
                # Rewind before every attempt: a retry re-sends the same file
                # object, whose read position may have advanced past a
                # partial read from a prior attempt that timed out mid-upload.
                fh.seek(0)
                # raise_on_error=False here regardless of the caller's setting: this
                # endpoint's error body is {"data": {"message", "errors", "task_id"}},
                # not the {"_error": {"message": ...}} shape APIClientBase._handle_error
                # expects — letting it auto-raise would surface the raw dict repr
                # instead of the server's actual validation message. We parse the
                # real body ourselves below and raise a clean error from it instead.
                return self.client.post_multipart(
                    endpoint=endpoint,
                    data=data,
                    files={"file": (file_path.name, fh, "text/csv")},
                    raise_on_error=False,
                )

            response = retrying(_do_request)

        if not (200 <= response.status_code < 300):
            if raise_on_error:
                detail = self._import_error_detail(response)
                error_cls = err.HTTP_ERRORS_MAP.get(response.status_code, err.APIError)
                raise error_cls(f"Classification import failed (status {response.status_code}): {detail}")
            try:
                return response.json()
            except ValueError:
                return {"data": {"message": response.text[:2000], "errors": None, "task_id": None}}

        try:
            payload = response.json()
        except ValueError as e:
            raise err.APIError(
                f"Classification import returned status {response.status_code} but the "
                f"response body isn't JSON — this is unexpected for a success status; check "
                f"the server logs. Response snippet: {response.text[:1000]}"
            ) from e

        if validate:
            return ClassificationImportResponse.model_validate(payload)
        return payload

    def _import_error_detail(self, response) -> str:
        """Best-effort extraction of an error detail from a failed import response.

        The endpoint normally returns JSON (``{"data": {"message", "errors", ...}}``)
        even on failure, but a genuine *unhandled* server-side exception (as
        opposed to a validation failure the view catches) bypasses that and
        returns Django's plain HTML error page instead — calling
        ``response.json()`` on that raises ``JSONDecodeError``. This falls
        back to a text snippet in that case so the caller still gets a clear
        error instead of an opaque JSON-parsing traceback.

        Args:
            response: The raw ``httpx.Response`` from the failed request.

        Returns:
            A human-readable detail string.
        """
        try:
            payload = response.json()
        except ValueError:
            hint = ""
            if response.status_code == 500:
                hint = (
                    " Trapper (v1 and v2) answers a table that fails validation with a bare 500, because "
                    "it cannot serialize its validation report. Check the CSV against the project: "
                    "every scientificName must belong to the project's classificator, each _id must "
                    "be a classification of the project, and classificationMethod should be present."
                )
            return f"non-JSON response (likely an unhandled server error):{hint} {response.text[:1000]}"

        block = payload.get("data", {}) if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}
        message = block.get("message") or "Classification import failed"
        errors = block.get("errors")
        return f"{message}: {errors}" if errors else message

def import_classifications(
        self,
        project_id: int,
        file: str | Path,
        approve: bool = True,
        import_bboxes: bool = True,
        import_expert_classifications: bool = True,
        import_ai_classifications: bool = False,
        overwrite_attrs: bool = False,
        ai_provider_id: int | str | None = None,
        validate: bool = True,
        check_table: bool = True,
        split: bool = False,
        delay: float = 1.0,
        chunk_size: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES,
        retry_attempts: int = 3,
        retry_min_wait: float = 1.0,
        retry_max_wait: float = 10.0,
        raise_on_error: bool = True,
) -> Union[
    ClassificationImportResponse, Dict[str, Any],
    List[Union[ClassificationImportResponse, Dict[str, Any]]],
]:
    """Import expert/AI observations from a CSV file into a classification project.

    Posts to ``media_classification/api/classifications/import/``. The CSV
    must follow the internal Trapper format and contain an ``_id`` column.
    Depending on server configuration the import runs synchronously or is
    scheduled as a Celery task, in which case the response carries a
    ``task_id`` instead of a final result message.

    Args:
        project_id: Classification project primary key.
        file: Path to the observations CSV file to upload.
        approve: Mark imported classifications as approved.
        import_bboxes: Import bounding boxes present in the ``bboxes`` column.
        import_expert_classifications: Import rows with classificationMethod = human.
        import_ai_classifications: Import rows with classificationMethod = machine.
            Requires ``ai_provider_id``.
        overwrite_attrs: Overwrite existing classification attributes when
            approving imported AI classifications. **Trapper v1 only**: v2 removed
            the option, so ``True`` raises ``UnsupportedVersionError`` there.
        ai_provider_id: AI provider primary key. Required when
            ``import_ai_classifications=True``.
        check_table: Check the table locally first (required columns, ``sex`` values) and
            raise ``ValueError`` instead of sending a table Trapper would reject with a bare 500.
        validate: Whether to validate the response with Pydantic.
        split: Instead of uploading ``file`` in one request, split it into
            several smaller, self-contained CSV chunks (each repeating the
            header row) and import them one request at a time, sleeping
            ``delay`` seconds between uploads. Unlike
            :meth:`~trapper_client.components.locations.LocationsComponent.import_locations`,
            this endpoint is a real REST API that can usually take a full
            file in one request — this is only useful as a workaround for
            very large CSVs that hit request-size limits (this server's
            ``DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE``/reverse-proxy limits) or time
            out. There is no real chunked/resumable upload protocol here
            (see :mod:`trapper_client.csv_chunking`).
        delay: Seconds to sleep between chunk uploads when ``split=True``.
            Ignored otherwise.
        chunk_size: Maximum size in bytes of each chunk when ``split=True``.
            Ignored otherwise. Defaults to 512 KiB.
        retry_attempts: Maximum number of attempts (first try + retries)
            per chunk/file upload when the request fails with a
            network-level error (read timeout, connection reset, ...) —
            the failure mode expected when a chunk is still too large or
            slow for the server. Does not retry on HTTP error responses
            (those are validation failures a retry can't fix). Set to
            ``1`` to disable retrying.
        retry_min_wait: Minimum exponential backoff delay in seconds
            between retry attempts.
        retry_max_wait: Maximum exponential backoff delay in seconds
            between retry attempts.
        raise_on_error: Whether to raise mapped API exceptions (e.g. missing
            project/AI provider, or invalid CSV rows returned as a 400).
            With ``split=True``, raises as soon as one chunk fails rather
            than uploading the rest.

    Returns:
        ``ClassificationImportResponse`` when ``validate=True``, otherwise
        the raw response dict. When ``split=True``, a list with one such
        result per chunk (in file order) instead of a single result.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``import_ai_classifications=True`` but ``ai_provider_id`` is not set.
        err.APIError: If the import fails (a 4xx/5xx response) and
            ``raise_on_error=True``. The exception message includes the
            server's actual ``data.message``/``data.errors`` (e.g. Django
            form errors per field) when the response is JSON — but a
            genuine unhandled server-side exception (as opposed to a
            validation failure) returns Django's plain HTML error page
            instead, with no JSON body at all; this method detects that
            case and raises a clear error with a text snippet rather than
            crashing on ``response.json()``.

    Example::

        result = client.classification_results.import_classifications(
            project_id=7, file="/tmp/observations.csv",
        )
        print(result.data.message, result.data.task_id)

        # A very large CSV, uploaded in <=512 KiB chunks, 2s apart:
        results = client.classification_results.import_classifications(
            project_id=7, file="/tmp/huge_observations.csv",
            split=True, delay=2,
        )
    """
    if import_ai_classifications and ai_provider_id is None:
        raise ValueError("ai_provider_id is required when import_ai_classifications=True")
    if check_table:
        self._check_table(Path(file))
    if overwrite_attrs:
        # Trapper v2's import view no longer reads it, so it would be dropped silently.
        self._require_version("v1", feature="classification_results.import_classifications(overwrite_attrs=True)")

    data: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "project_id": project_id,
        "approve": approve,
        "import_bboxes": import_bboxes,
        "import_expert_classifications": import_expert_classifications,
    }
    if overwrite_attrs:
        data["overwrite_attrs"] = True
    if import_ai_classifications:
        # Sent only when True: the server reads this flag from the raw
        # request body *before* running it through form validation, as a
        # plain Python truthy check — a literal "False" string sent over
        # multipart would still be truthy there.
        data["import_ai_classifications"] = True
        data["ai_provider_id"] = ai_provider_id

    retrying = retrying_for_chunk_upload(retry_attempts, retry_min_wait, retry_max_wait)

    if not split:
        return self._import_classifications_once(data, Path(file), validate, raise_on_error, retrying)

    chunk_paths = split_csv_by_size(file, max_bytes=chunk_size)
    try:
        results = []
        for i, chunk_path in enumerate(chunk_paths):
            results.append(
                self._import_classifications_once(data, chunk_path, validate, raise_on_error, retrying)
            )
            if i < len(chunk_paths) - 1:
                time.sleep(delay)
        return results
    finally:
        for chunk_path in chunk_paths:
            chunk_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

class ClassificationsMapComponent(TrapperComponent[ClassificationMap]):
    """
    Component for ``/media_classification/api/classifications_map/``.

    Retrieve and filter resources pending classification for a given project.

    Main endpoints:
    - ``GET /media_classification/api/classifications_map``: List of resources to classify (paginated)

    |----------------|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

    | owner          | boolean                  | true = resources where user is owner/manager                               |
    | deployment     | list of PKs              | Filter by deployment PKs                                                   |
    | collection     | list of PKs              | Filter by collection PKs                                                   |

    | classified     | boolean                  | Filter by whether resource has been classified by humans                   |
    | classified_ai  | boolean                  | Filter by whether resource has been classified by AI                       |
    | approved       | boolean                  | Whether classification is FINAL approved                                   |
    | species        | list of PKs              | Filter by species PKs                                                      |

    Returns a paginated list of resources pending classification with support for

class ClassificatorsComponent(TrapperComponent[Classificator]):
    """
    Component for ``/media_classification/api/classificators/``.

    Retrieve and filter classificators (AI/human classifier configurations) from Trapper.

    Main endpoints:
    - ``GET /media_classification/api/classificators``: List of classificators (paginated)
    - ``GET /media_classification/api/classificators/{pk}``: Single classificator detail

    **Available filter fields:**

    | Parameter  | Type    | Description                               |
    |------------|---------|-------------------------------------------|
    | owner      | boolean | true = classificators owned by the user   |
    | search     | string  | Search by name or description             |

    Returns a paginated list of classificators with support for filtering
    through query parameters.
    """

    endpoint = "/media_classification/api/classificators"
    schema = Classificator
    create_endpoint = "media_classification/classificator/create/"
    _CREATED_RE = re.compile(r"/classificator/update/(\d+)/")

    def create(
        self,
        classificator: ClassificatorCreate,
        *,
        raise_on_error: bool = True,
    ) -> Classificator | None:
        """Create a classificator (**Trapper v1 only**).

        The REST API is read-only for classificators, so this simulates the classic web form
        ``media_classification/classificator/create/`` with cookie/session authentication, as
        :meth:`~trapper_client.components.research_projects.ResearchProjectsComponent.create` does.
        The account that logs in becomes the owner.

        Trapper silently drops a species primary key that does not exist: a classificator whose
        ``species`` are all unknown ends up accepting every species. Check the keys against
        ``client.species`` first when it matters.

        Only the standard attributes are covered: species, tracked species, the optional
        attributes (sex, age, ...) and the layout. Custom and predefined attributes are not.

        Warning:
            It depends on an unversioned HTML form, and needs ``user_name``/``user_password`` (the
            *email* on servers that log in by email): a token alone cannot authenticate it.

        Args:
            classificator: A :class:`~trapper_client.schemas.classificators.ClassificatorCreate`,
                which validates it before anything is sent.
            raise_on_error: Raise ``APIError`` when the server rejects the form (the default);
                with ``False`` return ``None`` instead.

        Returns:
            The created classificator, or ``None`` when the server rejected the form and
            ``raise_on_error=False``.

        Raises:
            TypeError: ``classificator`` is not a ``ClassificatorCreate``.
            err.UnsupportedVersionError: On Trapper v2.
            err.APIError: The server rejected the form (a name already in use, unknown species,
                ...) or redirected to its login page.

        Example::

            clf = client.classificators.create(
                ClassificatorCreate(
                    name="Iberian mammals",
                    species=[12, 15, 40],
                    tracked_species=[40],
                    sex=True,
                    age=True,
                )
            )
        """
        self._require_version("v1", feature="classificators.create()")
        if not isinstance(classificator, ClassificatorCreate):
            raise TypeError(
                f"create() takes a ClassificatorCreate, not {type(classificator).__name__}; "
                "build one with ClassificatorCreate(...) or ClassificatorCreate.model_validate(data)"
            )

        response = self._submit_create_form(
            self.create_endpoint, classificator.to_form(), "Classificator", raise_on_error,
            field_prefix="classificator-",
        )
        if response is None:
            return None
        # Trapper redirects to the update page of the classificator it has just saved
        created = self._CREATED_RE.search(response.headers.get("location") or "")
        return self.find(int(created.group(1))) if created else None

Bases: TrapperComponent[Collection]

Component for the storage/api/collections resource.

Retrieve, filter, and export collection data from Trapper.

Main endpoints:

  • GET /storage/api/collections: Paginated list of accessible collections
  • GET /storage/api/collections/{id}: Single collection detail
  • GET /storage/api/collections_ondemand: On-demand collections for current user, paginated (Trapper v1 only: 404 on v2)
  • GET /storage/api/collections_map: Same fields as the list, but one plain list: not paginated (page_size is ignored)
  • GET /storage/api/collections_append: Collections the user can append resources to, one plain list of pk and name only (not paginated)
  • POST /storage/api/collection/process/: Trigger processing of an FTP-uploaded collection

The paginated and the plain endpoints are read through the same methods (where_map(), get_append(), ...): the plain ones are wrapped as a single page.

Available filter fields:

  • pk (list of PKs): Filter by specific collection PKs
  • status (choice): Private, OnDemand, Public or Archived, in any case (:class:~trapper_client.enums.CollectionStatus); any other value raises ValueError
  • owner (boolean): true = only collections owned/managed by current user
  • owners (list of PKs): Filter by one or more owner user PKs
  • research_projects (list of PKs): Filter by one or more research project PKs
  • locations_map (list of PKs): Filter via resources__deployment__location (v1 only)
  • search (string): Full-text search across name and owner__username

Examples:

# Retrieve all collections (lazy iteration)
for col in client.collections.where():
    print(col)

# Filter by owner
for col in client.collections.where(owner=True):
    print(col)

# Filter by research project
for col in client.collections.where(research_projects=3):
    print(col)

# Single page
page = client.collections.get(page=1, page_size=25)
print(page.pagination.count)

# Single collection by PK
col = client.collections.find(42)

# Lazy iteration over resources within a collection (see ResourcesComponent)
for res in client.resources.where_by_collection(collection_pk=3):
    print(res)

# Export resources of a collection to CSV
client.resources.export(file="/tmp/resources.csv", collections=3)
