    def download_many(
        self,
        resources: Iterable[Resource],
        directory: str | Path,
        kind: Literal["original", "preview", "thumbnail"] = "original",
        skip_existing: bool = True,
        on_error: Literal["continue", "raise"] = "continue",
        progress_callback: Callable[[str, Dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
        total: int | None = None,
        retry_attempts: int = 3,
        retry_min_wait: float = 1.0,
        retry_max_wait: float = 10.0,
    ) -> DownloadReport:
        """Download the files of some resources into one folder.

        Each one is saved as ``<name><extension>`` (the extension comes from the resource's ``mime``), with ``-<pk>`` added
        when two resources share a name. A preview or a thumbnail, which Trapper makes as JPEG, is
        ``<name>-preview.jpg`` or ``<name>-thumbnail.jpg``, so that they can share a folder with the originals.
        Trapper has no endpoint for this: it is :meth:`download` once per resource (so the same requirements apply:
        ``user_name``/``user_password``), with a report, and it carries on after a failure by default.

        Args:
            resources: The resources to download (a list, or the lazy ``where()`` iterator).
            directory: The folder; it is created.
            kind: ``"original"``, ``"preview"`` or ``"thumbnail"``.
            skip_existing: Leave alone a file that is already there, so that a run can be repeated after an
                interruption. A file that was cut never exists under its final name (it is a ``.part`` first).
            on_error: ``"continue"`` (default) records the failure in the report and goes on; ``"raise"`` stops at the
                first one.
            progress_callback: ``callback(event, data)``, called with ``"downloaded"``, ``"skipped"`` or ``"failed"`` and
                ``{"resource": ..., "path": ..., "index": n, "total": ...}`` (``"error"`` too, for a failure).
            total: How many resources there are, if known, for the callback.
            retry_attempts: Attempts for each file, the first one included (see :meth:`download`).
            retry_min_wait: Minimum backoff in seconds.
            retry_max_wait: Maximum backoff in seconds.

        Returns:
            A :class:`DownloadReport`.

        Raises:
            ValueError: ``kind`` or ``on_error`` is not valid, or ``user_name``/``user_password`` are missing.
        """
        if kind not in self.media_fields:
            raise ValueError(f"kind must be one of {', '.join(self.media_fields)}, not {kind!r}")
        if on_error not in ("continue", "raise"):
            raise ValueError("on_error must be 'continue' or 'raise'")
        self.client.session_login()

        folder = Path(directory)
        folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        report = DownloadReport(directory=folder)
        used: set[str] = set()

        def notify(event: str, resource: Resource, index: int, **extra: Any) -> None:
            if progress_callback:
                progress_callback(event, {"resource": resource, "index": index, "total": total, **extra})

        for index, resource in enumerate(resources, start=1):
            target = folder / self._file_name(resource, kind, used)
            try:
                if skip_existing and target.exists():
                    report.skipped.append(target)
                    notify("skipped", resource, index, path=target)
                    continue
                self.download(resource.pk, target, kind=kind, retry_attempts=retry_attempts,
                              retry_min_wait=retry_min_wait, retry_max_wait=retry_max_wait)
            except Exception as exc:
                if on_error == "raise":
                    raise
                report.failed[resource.pk] = str(exc)
                notify("failed", resource, index, path=target, error=exc)
                continue
            report.downloaded.append(target)
            notify("downloaded", resource, index, path=target)
        return report

    @staticmethod
    def _file_name(resource: Resource, kind: str, used: set[str]) -> str:
        """``<name><extension>`` for a resource, unique among ``used`` (it is added to it)."""
        if kind == "original":
            extension = mimetypes.guess_extension((resource.mime or "").split(";")[0].strip()) or ""
            extension = ".jpg" if extension == ".jpe" else extension
        else:
            extension = ".jpg"
        name = safe_filename(resource.name, fallback=f"resource-{resource.pk}")
        if kind != "original":
            name = f"{name}-{kind}"          # next to the original, not over it
        if extension and name.lower().endswith(extension.lower()):
            name, extension = name[: -len(extension)], name[-len(extension):]       # keep its own spelling
        candidate = f"{name}{extension}"
        if candidate.lower() in used:
            candidate = f"{name}-{resource.pk}{extension}"
        used.add(candidate.lower())
        return candidate

def download_many(
    self,
    resources: Iterable[Resource],
    directory: str | Path,
    kind: Literal["original", "preview", "thumbnail"] = "original",
    skip_existing: bool = True,
    on_error: Literal["continue", "raise"] = "continue",
    progress_callback: Callable[[str, Dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
    total: int | None = None,
    retry_attempts: int = 3,
    retry_min_wait: float = 1.0,
    retry_max_wait: float = 10.0,
) -> DownloadReport:
    """Download the files of some resources into one folder.

    Each one is saved as ``<name><extension>`` (the extension comes from the resource's ``mime``), with ``-<pk>`` added
    when two resources share a name. A preview or a thumbnail, which Trapper makes as JPEG, is
    ``<name>-preview.jpg`` or ``<name>-thumbnail.jpg``, so that they can share a folder with the originals.
    Trapper has no endpoint for this: it is :meth:`download` once per resource (so the same requirements apply:
    ``user_name``/``user_password``), with a report, and it carries on after a failure by default.

    Args:
        resources: The resources to download (a list, or the lazy ``where()`` iterator).
        directory: The folder; it is created.
        kind: ``"original"``, ``"preview"`` or ``"thumbnail"``.
        skip_existing: Leave alone a file that is already there, so that a run can be repeated after an
            interruption. A file that was cut never exists under its final name (it is a ``.part`` first).
        on_error: ``"continue"`` (default) records the failure in the report and goes on; ``"raise"`` stops at the
            first one.
        progress_callback: ``callback(event, data)``, called with ``"downloaded"``, ``"skipped"`` or ``"failed"`` and
            ``{"resource": ..., "path": ..., "index": n, "total": ...}`` (``"error"`` too, for a failure).
        total: How many resources there are, if known, for the callback.
        retry_attempts: Attempts for each file, the first one included (see :meth:`download`).
        retry_min_wait: Minimum backoff in seconds.
        retry_max_wait: Maximum backoff in seconds.

    Returns:
        A :class:`DownloadReport`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``kind`` or ``on_error`` is not valid, or ``user_name``/``user_password`` are missing.
    """
    if kind not in self.media_fields:
        raise ValueError(f"kind must be one of {', '.join(self.media_fields)}, not {kind!r}")
    if on_error not in ("continue", "raise"):
        raise ValueError("on_error must be 'continue' or 'raise'")
    self.client.session_login()

    folder = Path(directory)
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    report = DownloadReport(directory=folder)
    used: set[str] = set()

    def notify(event: str, resource: Resource, index: int, **extra: Any) -> None:
        if progress_callback:
            progress_callback(event, {"resource": resource, "index": index, "total": total, **extra})

    for index, resource in enumerate(resources, start=1):
        target = folder / self._file_name(resource, kind, used)
        try:
            if skip_existing and target.exists():
                report.skipped.append(target)
                notify("skipped", resource, index, path=target)
                continue
            self.download(resource.pk, target, kind=kind, retry_attempts=retry_attempts,
                          retry_min_wait=retry_min_wait, retry_max_wait=retry_max_wait)
        except Exception as exc:
            if on_error == "raise":
                raise
            report.failed[resource.pk] = str(exc)
            notify("failed", resource, index, path=target, error=exc)
            continue
        report.downloaded.append(target)
        notify("downloaded", resource, index, path=target)
    return report

            return None

        "individualPositionRadius", "individualPositionAngle", "individualSpeed",
        "bboxX", "bboxY", "bboxWidth", "bboxHeight",
        "classificationProbability", "count", "countNew",
        mode="before",
    )
    @classmethod
    def empty_numeric_to_none(cls, v):
        if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip() == "":
            return None
        return v

    @field_validator("classificationTimestamp", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def empty_datetime_to_none(cls, v):
        if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip() == "":
            return None
        return v

    @field_validator("bboxes", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def parse_bboxes(cls, v):
        if v is None or (isinstance(v, str) and v.strip() == ""):
            return None
        if isinstance(v, str):
            parsed = json.loads(v)
            # Trapper can write a null among the boxes: [[x, y, w, h], null].
            if isinstance(parsed, list):
                parsed = [b for b in parsed if b is not None]
            if not parsed:
                return None
            if all(isinstance(n, (int, float)) and not isinstance(n, bool) for n in parsed) and len(parsed) == 4:
                # Trapper v2 stores one box per observation, flat: [x, y, w, h].
                return [BBox(x=parsed[0], y=parsed[1], width=parsed[2], height=parsed[3])]
            if isinstance(parsed[0], (list, type(None))):
                # Trapper v1 stores a list of boxes. It sometimes sends a null (or short) entry among them.
                boxes = [BBox(x=b[0], y=b[1], width=b[2], height=b[3])
                         for b in parsed if isinstance(b, (list, tuple)) and len(b) >= 4]
                return boxes or None
            return parsed
        return v

class ClassificationProjectCreate(BaseModel):
    """What it takes to create a classification project
    (``client.classification_projects.create()``).

    ``ClassificationProject`` is what the API answers (it names the research project, not its pk);
    this is what the creation form asks. Unknown fields are rejected, so a typo fails here and not
    silently on the server.

    The research project and the classificator can be given as the objects the SDK returns
    (``ResearchProject``, ``Classificator``) or as their primary keys; the model keeps the
    primary keys.

    The project starts *ongoing*, and the account that creates it becomes its owner and
    administrator. Collections are added afterwards with ``add_collections()``.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", str_strip_whitespace=True)

    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=255)
    research_project: int | ResearchProject = Field(description="The research project, or its primary key.")
    classificator: int | Classificator = Field(description="The classificator, or its primary key.")
    members: List[ClassificationProjectMember] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="The users that join the project besides its creator, who is its administrator.",
    )

    @field_validator("research_project", "classificator")
    @classmethod
    def _primary_key(cls, value: int | ResearchProject | Classificator) -> int:
        """Keep the primary key (an object is replaced by its ``pk``)."""
        pk = value if isinstance(value, int) else value.pk
        if pk <= 0:
            raise ValueError("the primary key must be positive")
        return pk

    @field_validator("members")
    @classmethod
    def _one_role_per_user(cls, value: List[ClassificationProjectMember]) -> List[ClassificationProjectMember]:
        """Trapper refuses a user that appears twice in a project."""
        seen: set = set()
        repeated = sorted({m.user for m in value if m.user in seen or seen.add(m.user)})
        if repeated:
            raise ValueError(f"users {repeated} appear more than once in members")
        return value

    def role_rows(self) -> List[tuple]:
        """The members as the ``(user pk, role)`` pairs of the form's role rows."""
        return [(m.user, int(m.role)) for m in self.members]

    def to_form(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """The fields of Trapper's ``media_classification/project/create/`` form."""
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "research_project": self.research_project,
            "classificator": self.classificator,
            "status": 1,  # ongoing: the form hides the field and posts this value on creation
        }

class ClassificatorCreate(BaseModel):
    """What it takes to create a classificator (``client.classificators.create()``).

    ``Classificator`` is what the API answers (it leaves out the species and the standard
    attributes); this is what the creation form asks. Unknown fields are rejected, so a typo fails
    here and not silently on the server.

    ``species`` limits the species a classifier can choose from (empty: every species). Both lists
    take the species themselves (``Species``, as ``client.species`` returns them) or their
    primary keys; the model keeps the primary keys.
    ``tracked_species`` are the ones Trapper watches: classifying one of them notifies the
    administrators of the project. Observation type, count and "is setup" are always on.

    Custom and predefined attributes are not part of this model.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", str_strip_whitespace=True)

    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=255, description="Unique.")
    template: Annotated[ClassificatorTemplate, choice(ClassificatorTemplate)] = ClassificatorTemplate.INLINE
    species: list[int | Species] = Field(
        default_factory=list, description="Species (or their pks); empty = every species."
    )
    tracked_species: list[int | Species] = Field(
        default_factory=list, description="Species (or their pks) to watch."
    )
    sex: bool = False
    age: bool = False
    count_new: bool = False
    behaviour: bool = False
    individual_id: bool = False
    classification_confidence: bool = False

    @field_validator("species", "tracked_species")
    @classmethod
    def _primary_keys(cls, value: list[int | Species]) -> list[int]:
        """Keep the primary keys (a ``Species`` is replaced by its ``pk``), without repeats."""
        pks = [item.pk if isinstance(item, Species) else item for item in value]
        if any(pk <= 0 for pk in pks):
            raise ValueError("species primary keys must be positive")
        return list(dict.fromkeys(pks))

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _tracked_within_species(self) -> "ClassificatorCreate":
        extra = [pk for pk in self.tracked_species if self.species and pk not in self.species]
        if extra:
            raise ValueError(
                f"tracked_species {extra} are not in species: a classifier can only be warned about "
                "species it can choose"
            )
        return self

    def to_form(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """The fields of Trapper's ``classificator/create/`` form (all prefixed ``classificator-``)."""
        data: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "classificator-name": self.name,
            "classificator-template": self.template.value,
            "classificator-species": ",".join(str(pk) for pk in self.species),
            "classificator-tracked_species": ",".join(str(pk) for pk in self.tracked_species),
        }
        for flag in ("sex", "age", "count_new", "behaviour", "individual_id", "classification_confidence"):
            if getattr(self, flag):
                data[f"classificator-{flag}"] = "on"      # a checkbox is posted only when ticked
        return data

class DeploymentExport(BaseModel):
    """Schema for deployment export endpoint rows.

    Maps the export CSV field names (camelCase) to Python-friendly names.
    Fields marked as optional may be absent depending on the Trapper deployment.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow", populate_by_name=True)

    pk: int | None = Field(None, alias="_id")
    deployment_id: str | None = Field(None, alias="deploymentID")
    location_id: str | None = Field(None, alias="locationID")
    location_name: str | None = Field(None, alias="locationName")

    latitude: float | None = Field(None, alias="latitude")
    longitude: float | None = Field(None, alias="longitude")
    coordinate_uncertainty: float | None = Field(None, alias="coordinateUncertainty")

    start_date: datetime | str | None = Field(None, alias="deploymentStart")
    end_date: datetime | str | None = Field(None, alias="deploymentEnd")

    @field_validator("start_date", "end_date", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _dates_as_datetimes(cls, v):
        return read_datetime(v)

    setup_by: str | None = Field(None, alias="setupBy")
    camera_id: str | None = Field(None, alias="cameraID")
    camera_model: str | None = Field(None, alias="cameraModel")
    camera_interval: int | None = Field(None, alias="cameraDelay")
    camera_height: float | None = Field(None, alias="cameraHeight")
    camera_depth: float | None = Field(None, alias="cameraDepth")
    camera_tilt: float | None = Field(None, alias="cameraTilt")
    camera_heading: float | None = Field(None, alias="cameraHeading")
    detection_distance: float | None = Field(None, alias="detectionDistance")

    bait_type: str | None = Field(None, alias="baitType")
    bait_use: bool | None = Field(None, alias="baitUse")

    timestamp_issues: bool | None = Field(None, alias="timestampIssues")
    feature_type: str | None = Field(None, alias="featureType")
    habitat: str | None = Field(None, alias="habitat")
    session: str | None = Field(None, alias="session")
    array: str | None = Field(None, alias="array")
    comments: str | None = Field(None, alias="deploymentComments")
    tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _split_groups_and_tags(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
        """Read ``session``, ``array``, ``tags`` and ``bait_type`` from the two columns that hold them.

        Trapper's export has no column for any of those four. ``deploymentGroups`` holds the first two
        (``session:S | array:A``) and ``deploymentTags`` the tags, joined by `` | ``, with
        ``baitType:<value>`` appended when the deployment has a bait type. A value given by its own name
        wins, so a row that already has ``session`` or ``tags`` is left as it is.
        """
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            return data
        data = dict(data)
        groups = data.pop("deploymentGroups", None)
        tags = data.pop("deploymentTags", None)
        if isinstance(groups, str):
            for part in groups.split("|"):
                key, sep, value = part.partition(":")
                key, value = key.strip(), value.strip()
                if sep and key in ("session", "array") and value and not data.get(key):
                    data[key] = value
        if isinstance(tags, str) and "tags" not in data:
            plain = []
            for name in (t.strip() for t in tags.split("|")):
                if not name:
                    continue
                if name.startswith("baitType:"):
                    if not data.get("bait_type") and not data.get("baitType"):
                        data["bait_type"] = name[len("baitType:"):].strip()
                else:
                    plain.append(name)
            data["tags"] = plain
        return data

    @field_validator("pk", "camera_interval", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _parse_int(cls, v):
        if v == "" or v is None:
            return None
        try:
            return int(float(v))
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            return None

    @field_validator(
        "latitude", "longitude", "coordinate_uncertainty",
        "camera_height", "camera_depth", "camera_tilt", "camera_heading",
        "detection_distance", mode="before",
    )
    @classmethod
    def _parse_float(cls, v):
        if v == "" or v is None:
            return None
        try:
            return float(v)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            return None

    @field_validator("timestamp_issues", "bait_use", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _parse_bool(cls, v):
        if v == "" or v is None:
            return None
        if isinstance(v, bool):
            return v
        if isinstance(v, str):
            return v.strip().lower() in ("true", "1", "yes")
        return bool(v)

class ResearchProjectCreate(BaseModel):
    """What it takes to create a research project (``client.research_projects.create()``).

    Trapper's REST API does not return most of these fields (see ``TRAPPER_API_IMPROVEMENTS.md``),
    so this is an input model: ``ResearchProject`` is what the API answers, this is what the
    creation form asks. The limits are the ones of Trapper's model, and unknown fields are
    rejected, so a typo fails here and not silently on the server.

    The four choice fields take an enumeration member, its number or its label::

        ResearchProjectCreate(name="Doñana mammals", acronym="DONMAM",
                               sampling_design=SamplingDesign.TARGETED, bait_use="scent")
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", str_strip_whitespace=True)

    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=255, description="Unique.")
    acronym: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=10, description="Unique.")
    sampling_design: Annotated[SamplingDesign, choice(SamplingDesign)] = SamplingDesign.SIMPLE_RANDOM
    sensor_method: Annotated[SensorMethod, choice(SensorMethod)] = SensorMethod.ACTIVITY_DETECTION
    animal_types: Annotated[AnimalTypes, choice(AnimalTypes)] = AnimalTypes.UNMARKED
    bait_use: Annotated[BaitUse, choice(BaitUse)] = BaitUse.NONE
    event_interval: int = Field(default=0, ge=0, description="Seconds.")
    keywords: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    abstract: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=2000)
    methods: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=2000)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=2000)
    members: list[ResearchProjectMember] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="The users that join the project besides its creator, who is its administrator.",
    )

    @field_validator("keywords")
    @classmethod
    def _clean_keywords(cls, value: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        """Trim the keywords and drop the empty ones.

        A keyword may hold spaces and commas (they are sent quoted, see ``to_form()``), but not a
        double quote: Trapper cannot represent it and would drop it.
        """
        keywords = [k.strip() for k in value if k and k.strip()]
        if any('"' in k for k in keywords):
            raise ValueError("a keyword cannot contain a double quote")
        return keywords

    @field_validator("members")
    @classmethod
    def _one_role_per_user(cls, value: list[ResearchProjectMember]) -> list[ResearchProjectMember]:
        """Trapper refuses a user that appears twice in a project."""
        seen: set[int] = set()
        repeated = sorted({m.user for m in value if m.user in seen or seen.add(m.user)})
        if repeated:
            raise ValueError(f"users {repeated} appear more than once in members")
        return value

    def role_rows(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        """The members as the ``(user pk, role)`` pairs of the form's role rows."""
        return [(m.user, int(m.role)) for m in self.members]

    def to_form(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The fields of Trapper's ``research/project/create/`` form, as it expects them."""
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "acronym": self.acronym,
            "sampling_design": int(self.sampling_design),
            "sensor_method": int(self.sensor_method),
            "animal_types": int(self.animal_types),
            "bait_use": int(self.bait_use),
            "event_interval": self.event_interval,
            # each one quoted: without quotes Trapper splits "camera trap" into two keywords when it
            # is the only one (it splits on spaces when there is no comma), and on any comma
            "keywords": ", ".join(f'"{keyword}"' for keyword in self.keywords),
            "abstract": self.abstract or "",
            "methods": self.methods or "",
            "description": self.description or "",
        }

Bases: BaseModel

Schema for /tables/api/species items.

The server serializes the model's __str__() under the literal field name __str__ (DRF's SpeciesSerializer). That name is not usable as a Pydantic field, so it is exposed here as display_name via an alias.

Source code in src/trapper_client/schemas/species.py 
class Species(BaseModel):
    """Schema for ``/tables/api/species`` items.

    The server serializes the model's ``__str__()`` under the literal field
    name ``__str__`` (DRF's ``SpeciesSerializer``). That name is not usable
    as a Pydantic field, so it is exposed here as ``display_name`` via an
    alias.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    pk: int
    display_name: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, alias="__str__")
    english_name: Optional[str] = None
    latin_name: Optional[str] = None
    genus: Optional[str] = None
    family: Optional[str] = None

A single observation attribute returned by the User classifier.

Source code in src/trapper_client/schemas/user_classifications.py 
class UserObservationAttr(BaseModel):
    """A single observation attribute returned by the User classifier."""

    observation_type: str
    species: Optional[str] = None
    count: Optional[str] = None
    classification_confidence: Optional[str] = None

    @field_validator("observation_type", "species", "count", "classification_confidence", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _unwrap_value(cls, v: Any) -> Any:
        """Trapper v2 wraps each attribute as ``{"value": ...}``; v1 sends the bare value."""
        if isinstance(v, dict) and "value" in v:
            return v["value"]
        return v

docs.title: Export, scoped to a project
docs.text:
Unlike every other component, export() here has a different signature: it requires a classification_project_pk (the underlying endpoint needs one, and there's no unscoped export):

client.ai_classifications.export(
    classification_project_pk=7,
    file="ai_results.csv",
)

# Or get model instances instead of a file
records = client.ai_classifications.export(classification_project_pk=7, file=None)

Rows are parsed as either the CamtrapDP-flavoured or Trapper-flavoured export schema, depending on whether the server includes a Trapper-internal _id field.

Additional field on the export endpoint:

Parameter Type Default Description camtrapdp boolean True True = CamtrapDP standard rows, False = Trapper's internal format

docs.title: Classification Media
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — same code on both. See Trapper versions.

client.classification_media — media rows (with download URLs) for a classification project.

Endpoint: GET /media_classification/api/media/{project_pk}/.

Not directly usable via get()/where()

The endpoint needs a project_pk in its URL, so calling the generic get()/get_all()/where()/ all()/find() inherited from every component wouldn't work here — use the _project_media/ _collection_media methods below instead, all of which resolve the URL for you.

docs.title: What it represents
docs.text:
A classification project takes collections of resources and records what is in each one (its classification). client.classification_media is the media table of that project: one row per resource of the project, in the shape of the Camtrap DP media file (Trapper builds it from the project's final classification of each resource, from its source). It is not a list of every resource in Trapper: a resource that is in no classification project has no row here, and so no download URL with a token. For those, see Downloading the file in the resources guide.

Each row is a Media, the same eleven columns on Trapper v1 and v2:

Column What it is mediaID The primary key of the resource (Resource.pk) deploymentID The deployment's deployment_id text (don01-2024a), not its primary key captureMethod How the deployment captures (activityDetection in Trapper's data) timestamp date_recorded, with its UTC offset (2024-03-19T13:30:31+0100) filePath The URL to download the file, with the resource's token when the file is public (see below) filePublic True when filePath carries the token, False when it does not fileName The resource's name, without extension (don01-2024a_0004) fileMediatype Its MIME type (image/jpeg) exifData Always empty: Trapper does not fill it (from its source) favorite, mediaComments Flag and comments; empty in the data checked

How it arrives: the server sends the whole table as one gzip CSV and ignores paging. page_size has no effect, and page=2 returns the same rows as page=1, with pages=1. where_project_media() and get_all are fine with that; do not rely on page to walk it.

What is in each image is not here

The table describes the resources of the classification project and their files, not what they show. There is no animal, vehicle, species, count, sex or bounding box in a row: that is in the project's classification results (client.classification_results). A resource that is in no classification project has no row here either. To have both, join them by mediaID:

seen = {}
for obs in client.classification_results.where_project_results(7):
    seen.setdefault(obs.mediaID, []).append(obs.observationType)

for row in client.classification_media.where_project_media(7):
    print(row.fileName, seen.get(row.mediaID))      # don01-2024a_0004 ['animal']

The filters do look at the classification (species, observation_type, ...), so you can ask for the images with a lynx, but the row you get back does not say it is a lynx.

docs.title: Public and private files
docs.text:
filePath is always there, but only a public file has ?rt=<token> in it, and only that URL can be downloaded with no session. By default Trapper hides the images of humans and vehicles: their row has filePublic false and a URL without token, which answers 404. The extra parameters decide it:

  • private_human and private_vehicle (default hide): True hides the files whose observation is a human, or a vehicle; False shows them with their token.
  • private_species: meant to hide the files of some species (primary keys), but Trapper answers 500 with any value, an empty one included (checked on v1 and v2). Do not use it.
  • trapper_url_token: False leaves the token out of every URL, so all the rows are private.

Booleans: True, False, or the text

Trapper reads only the exact text True as true, and any other, true included, as false (so a client that sends a boolean the usual way gets the opposite). The SDK sends private_human, private_vehicle, trapper_url and trapper_url_token as True/False text itself: give a Python boolean, or the text true/false in any case. Anything else (1, "yes", None) is a ValueError before the request. Before this was done (issue #85), private_human=True showed the humans.

For example, with a project that has two images of humans (checked on Trapper v2, 28 rows):

cm = client.classification_media

# The default: humans and vehicles are private. 26 of the 28 rows are public.
rows = list(cm.where_project_media(7))
print(sum(r.filePublic for r in rows))                       # 26
print([r.fileName for r in rows if not r.filePublic])        # the two private ones: their URL has no token

# Treat humans and vehicles as public: every URL carries the token
rows = list(cm.where_project_media(7, private_human=False, private_vehicle=False))
print(sum(r.filePublic for r in rows))                       # 28

# Humans stay private, vehicles do not
rows = list(cm.where_project_media(7, private_human=True, private_vehicle=False))

# The same parameters go to the downloads: with the default, the private files are not downloaded
cm.download_project_media_files(7, "out/", private_human=False, private_vehicle=False)

Leave private_human as it is if you are going to share the rows or the files: by default the URL of a human carries no token, so the image cannot be downloaded with it.

A project table with nothing to show (a filter that leaves no rows, or a project the account cannot see) is answered by Trapper with a 400 ("Empty queryset or you have no permission..."), not an empty list. The SDK reads it as an empty result in get_*, where_*, export_* and the downloads (count 0, nothing to iterate, [], an empty file), as the classification list does. The 400 is also the answer to a missing permission, so a project that the account cannot see looks empty too; any other 400 (a wrong filter value) is still a BadRequestError.

docs.text:
Parameter Type Description owner boolean true = resources where the user is owner or manager deployment list of PKs Filter by deployment PKs collection list of PKs The pk of the link between the project and the collection (ClassificationProjectCollection), not the collection's pk. With where_project_media(collection=3), 3 is a link: on Trapper v1 it answers the rows of link 3, which can be another collection, and no error. To give the collection's pk use where_collection_media(), which translates it. Links are listed by classification_projects.get_all_project_collections() (link.pk, link.collection_pk) locations_map comma-separated PKs Filter by location PKs rdate_from / rdate_to date date_recorded range rtime_from / rtime_to HH:MM Time-of-day range on date_recorded ftype choice Filter by resource type (IMAGE, VIDEO, ...) classified boolean Classified by user (500 on Trapper v2 for this table) classified_ai boolean Classified by AI (500 on Trapper v2 for this table) approved boolean Classification approved. Works on both: Trapper v1 calls it status, and the SDK sends it as such there bboxes boolean Has bounding boxes species list of PKs Filter by species PKs observation_type choice Filter by observation type sex choice Filter by sex age choice Filter by age

Extra params (independent of filtering):

Parameter Type Default Description trapper_url bool True Read by Trapper but not used: the URL is always absolute (from its source) trapper_url_token bool True False leaves the token out of every URL (all the files are then private) private_human bool True True hides the files of humans (see Public and private files) private_vehicle bool True True hides the files of vehicles private_species list of PKs [] Meant to hide the files of those species; answers 500 with any value

docs.text:

page = client.classification_media.get_project_media(project_pk=7, page_size=200)

# Lazy iteration
for row in client.classification_media.where_project_media(project_pk=7, deployment=12):
    print(row)

# CSV export

# Find one media row by its media/resource ID

docs.text:
page = client.classification_media.get_collection_media(project_pk=7, collection_pk=5)

for row in client.classification_media.where_collection_media(project_pk=7, collection_pk=5):
    print(row)

    project_pk=7, collection_pk=5, file="collection_media.csv",

docs.title: Downloading the actual files
docs.text:
Each media row's filePath is an absolute, ready-to-download URL (it already carries the resource's access token) — required for private resources, since the underlying file-serving view isn't part of the DRF API and doesn't honor the Authorization header.

# Download every media file from a project
files = client.classification_media.download_project_media_files(
    project_pk=7, output_dir="media",
)

# Same, but scoped to a collection, in parallel, compressed into one ZIP
files = client.classification_media.download_collection_media_files(
    project_pk=7, collection_pk=5, output_dir="collection_media",
    parallel=True, compress=True,
)

# Download one file directly if you already have its URL
path = client.classification_media.download_media_file(
    file_url=row.filePath, file="media_4831.jpg",
)

Nothing but the URL is sent: no API token and no session, so it works with a token alone. The file is streamed to a temporary .part file that is moved into place when complete, so a failed download never leaves a half-written file. Network failures and 502/503/504 answers are retried with exponential backoff (retry_attempts, retry_min_wait, retry_max_wait); a 404 (a missing file or a token that is no longer valid) is a NotFoundError and is not retried.

docs.title: What the downloads of a project or a collection return
docs.text:
download_project_media_files() and download_collection_media_files() return the list of the paths that were downloaded (a DownloadedFiles, which is a list) and carry what happened to the rest:

files = client.classification_media.download_project_media_files(7, "media/")
print(len(files), "downloaded")
print(files.failed)        # {7: 'download of http://.../media/7/file/: the server answered 404', ...}
print(files.ok)            # False when something failed
  • A file that fails (after its retries) is in .failed ({media id: message}) and is logged; the rest go on. With on_error="raise" the first failure stops it. Before, a failure disappeared: with the default private_human the files of the humans (a row with no token) were left out and nothing said so.
  • skip_existing=True leaves a file that is already in the folder, so an interrupted run is repeated with the same call; those are in .skipped. Files are named media_<id>, with no extension.

docs.title: Classification Package
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — same code on both. See Trapper versions.

client.classification_package — generates (or reuses a cached) Camtrap DP data package for a classification project, and returns its download URL.

Endpoint: GET /media_classification/api/package/{project_pk}/.

Not directly usable via get()/where()

This is a single fixed-shape JSON response, not a paginated list — use get_project_package() below.

docs.title: Generating and downloading a package
docs.text:
response = client.classification_package.get_project_package(project_pk=7)

print(response.data.message)
print(response.data.package)  # absolute download URL, already carries its own one-time token

file_response = client.make_request(endpoint=response.data.package, method="GET")
with open("camtrapdp_project_7.zip", "wb") as f:
    f.write(file_response.content)

response.data.package's URL already carries a one-time access token (?rt=...) — download it as-is via client.make_request(), never re-request it through a component method.

There's also a ready-to-run script: examples/download_camtrapdp_for_classification_project.py.

docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description clear_cache bool False Force regeneration instead of reusing the cached package release bool False Mark the generated package as a release get_released bool False Return the latest already-published release instead export_format str "camtrapdp" Also accepts "trapper" (disables include_events) export_filetype str "csv.gz" File format for the data tables inside the package

docs.title: Classification Projects
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — except create(), add_collections() and remove_collection(), which are v1 only. See Trapper versions.

client.classification_projects — classification projects: the workspace where resources from one or more collections get classified against a classificator.

Endpoints:

  • GET /media_classification/api/projects (list + detail)
  • GET /media_classification/api/project/{project_pk}/collections (collections linked to a project)
  • GET /media_classification/api/collection/{collection_pk}/resources/ (classified resources within a project-collection link)

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description owner boolean true = projects where the user is owner, manager, or has any role status choice Filter by project status research_project PK Filter by research project FK search str Searches across name, owner username, research project name

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
for proj in client.classification_projects.all():
    print(proj)

client.classification_projects.export(file="cs_projects.csv")

See Usage for get(), get_all(), find() — same interface as every component.

docs.title: Collections linked to a project
docs.text:
Same family of methods as Research Projects, scoped to /media_classification/api/project/{project_pk}/collections:

page = client.classification_projects.get_project_collections(project_pk=60)
for col in client.classification_projects.where_project_collections(project_pk=60):
    print(col)
result = client.classification_projects.get_all_project_collections(project_pk=60)

col = client.classification_projects.find_project_collection(project_pk=60, pk=35)

link_pk = client.classification_projects.find_collection_in_project(
    project_pk=60, collection_pk=47,
)

pk/collection_pk here is a link pk, not the storage collection pk

The server's Classification.collection foreign key points to ClassificationProjectCollection (the row linking a project to a collection), not to the storage Collection itself. That link row has its own pk, and it's what every method below expects — passing the storage collection's pk instead will either 404 or silently return nothing.

How to get the right pk:

  • If you only know the project and the storage collection pk, resolve it with find_collection_in_project(project_pk, collection_pk) (shown above) — it iterates the project's links and returns the matching link pk, or None if that collection isn't linked to the project.
  • If you're already iterating get_project_collections()/where_project_collections(), each item's own .pk is the link pk you need — no extra lookup required.

This same link pk is also what the collection= filter expects on classifications, ai_classifications, user_classifications, classifications_map, and sequences. The one exception is classification_media, whose collection_pk is the real storage collection pk — it resolves the link pk for you internally.

docs.title: Classified resources within a project-collection link
docs.text:
This is the underlying data for the classification UI's resource browser: classified resources (with sequence and approval info) inside one project-collection link.

page = client.classification_projects.get_collection_resources(collection_pk=35)
for res in client.classification_projects.where_collection_resources(collection_pk=35):
    print(res)
result = client.classification_projects.get_all_collection_resources(collection_pk=35)

docs.title: Previous/next navigation around one resource
docs.text:
The server also supports a windowed, non-page-based pagination mode — the same one the classify UI uses for "previous/next" navigation — returning up to size resources on each side of a given resource, ordered by date_recorded:

page = client.classification_projects.get_collection_resources_around(
    collection_pk=35, resource_pk=4831, size=5,
)
print(page.pagination.total, page.pagination.filtered)  # not .count/.pages here
for res in page.results:
    print(res.pk, res.name)

docs.title: Creating a classification project (Trapper v1)
docs.text:
The REST API is read-only for classification projects, so create(), add_collections() and remove_collection() work around that by simulating Trapper's classic web forms via cookie/session auth, like import_locations(). On Trapper v2 they raise UnsupportedVersionError.

Not a stable API contract

They depend on unversioned HTML forms and need user_name/user_password (the account's email on servers that log in by email): a token alone cannot authenticate them.

from trapper_client import ClassificationProjectCreate

project = client.classification_projects.create(
    ClassificationProjectCreate(name="Doñana 2026", research_project=3, classificator=2)
)
print(project.pk, project.name, project.status)        # 12 Doñana 2026 Ongoing

create() takes a ClassificationProjectCreate, a Pydantic model. Building it validates the data before anything is sent: a name, and the research project and the classificator, each given as the object the SDK returns (ResearchProject, Classificator) or as its primary key, so the creations chain:

rp = client.research_projects.create(ResearchProjectCreate(name="Doñana mammals", acronym="DONMAM"))
clf = client.classificators.create(ClassificatorCreate(name="Iberian mammals"))
project = client.classification_projects.create(
    ClassificationProjectCreate(name="Doñana 2026", research_project=rp, classificator=clf)
)

To build the model from a dict, use ClassificationProjectCreate.model_validate(data). The project starts ongoing, and the account that logs in becomes its owner and administrator. The research project must be one the account can edit; otherwise Trapper rejects the form and create() raises APIError naming the field:

Classification project creation failed (status 200): research_project: Select a valid choice. That choice is not one of the available choices.

It returns the created project, or None if it cannot be read back (or the form was rejected and raise_on_error=False).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
As with research projects, the creator becomes the administrator and members adds the other users, each with a role:

from trapper_client import ClassificationProjectCreate, ClassificationProjectMember

project = client.classification_projects.create(
    ClassificationProjectCreate(
        name="Doñana 2026",
        research_project=rp,
        classificator=clf,
        members=[
            ClassificationProjectMember(user=ana, role="expert"),
            ClassificationProjectMember(user=7, role="collaborator"),
        ],
    )
)
print([(r.user, r.roles) for r in project.project_roles])
# [('Ana Romero', ['Expert']), ('rp_staff', ['Admin']), ('user7', ['Collaborator'])]

role is a ClassificationProjectRoleType, its number or its label (any case): ADMIN, EXPERT, COLLABORATOR, and ERROR_PROOF and CITIZEN, which belong to Trapper's citizen science features. user is a User from client.users or its primary key. A user cannot appear twice and the creator cannot be listed; both fail before anything is sent. The members can only be given when the project is created.

docs.title: Adding collections
docs.text:
A new project is empty. add_collections() links storage collections to it:

links = client.classification_projects.add_collections(project.pk, [1, 2])
print([(link.pk, link.collection_pk) for link in links])
  • The numbers you pass are the primary keys of the storage collections (Collection.pk), as in the rest of the SDK. The SDK works out the link records Trapper needs by itself.
  • A classification project can only use the collections of its research project, and the account must administer that research project. A collection that is not there raises ValueError before anything is sent. Linking a collection to a research project is a web action the SDK does not cover.
  • A collection that is already in the project is left as it is, so the call can be repeated.
  • It returns the project's link for each collection.

docs.title: Removing a collection
docs.text:
client.classification_projects.remove_collection(project.pk, 1)    # True; False if it was not linked

It deletes classifications

Unlinking is irreversible, and the classifications made on that collection in this project are deleted with the link. The collection and its resources are not touched.

docs.title: Classification Results Agg
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — same code on both. See Trapper versions.

client.classification_results_agg — aggregated classification results per deployment (counts, coordinates), for a classification project.

Endpoint: GET /media_classification/api/classifications/results/agg/{project_pk}/. Returns CSV (gzip) by default, or GeoJSON when geojson=True.

Not directly usable via get()/where()

The endpoint needs a project_pk in its URL — use get_project_results_agg()/ export_project_results_agg() below, which resolve the URL for you.

docs.title: Fetching a page
docs.text:
page = client.classification_results_agg.get_project_results_agg(project_pk=7)
for row in page.results:
    print(row.deploymentID, row.count, row.countNew)

docs.title: Exporting to CSV
docs.text:
client.classification_results_agg.export_project_results_agg(
    project_pk=7, file="agg_results.csv",
)

export_project_results_agg() only supports CSV — it raises ValueError if you pass geojson=True. For the GeoJSON variant, use get_project_results_agg(project_pk=7, geojson=True) directly instead (the response shape differs, so it isn't wrapped as a CSV export).

docs.title: Classifications
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — except import_classifications(overwrite_attrs=True), which is v1 only. See Trapper versions.

client.classification_results — the final classifications of a classification project. Its class is ClassificationResultsComponent (also known as ClassificationsComponent: the same class).

docs.title: What it represents
docs.text:
In a classification project every resource has one final classification: the record that holds the result for that resource (what it shows), taken from the classification someone made or imported and then approved (from Trapper's source). approved says whether that has happened; the resources nobody has classified have a final classification too, with the observation type unclassified. This component reads those records in three ways, each with its own shape (checked on Trapper v1 and v2):

List (where(), find()) Results table (where_project_results(), export_project_results()) Import One row per resource observation (a resource with two species has two rows) the _id of a final classification Species text ("European Rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus)"), no pk scientificName scientificName sex, lifeStage, behavior, bboxes not there yes yes Identifier pk, the primary key of the classification _id (only with camtrapdp=False); observationID is only the row number in the table you asked for (it changes with the filters) and is not in the list _id Needs a project for deployment and collection yes, in the URL yes

So to know what each image shows, use the results table; the list tells you which resources are classified and approved, and nothing more. Its dynamic_attrs carry only observation_type, species and count.

docs.title: What each thing is
docs.text:
• Classification: what one person (or the AI) decided about one resource, and it is a set of observations: zero (nothing classified yet), one, or several. Each user's classification of a resource is its own record (user_classifications, see User classifications); the final classification is the one record per resource that this component reads. When someone's classification is approved, the final one is taken from it (from Trapper's source and checked on v1 and v2): it is one classification chosen, copied, not a merge of several.
  • Observation: one thing seen in the resource, with its type (animal, human, blank, ...), species, count, sex, lifeStage and behavior. It is a row of the results table. An image with nothing in it has one (blank, or unclassified when nobody has looked).
  • Bounding box: an optional position of the observation in the image. It says where, not what: what is there is said by the observation, and who said it by classificationMethod (human or machine) and classifiedBy. The server versions store it differently, see Boxes below.
  • _id: the primary key of the final classification, the same as the pk of the list. It is the identifier of the classification, not of an observation: the rows of the same image share it (checked: a rabbit and a lynx in one image are two rows with the same _id). It is what the import needs.
  • observationID: only the number of the row in the table you asked for. It changes with the filters (the same observation is 4 in the whole table and 1 with sex=male) and with the format (on v1 the same observation is 4 with camtrapdp=False and 28 with camtrapdp=True), so it identifies nothing and cannot be compared between two requests. An observation has no identifier of its own: to find it again, use _id and the species.

docs.title: Several things in one image
docs.text: They are several observations of one classification, one row each, with the same _id and different observationID (checked on v1 and v2: a rabbit and a lynx in one image give two rows). Several animals of the same species are one observation with a count (a rabbit twice is count=2, one row). The boxes, which are optional, are stored differently by the two Trapper versions:

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
Trapper v1 Trapper v2 Stored per observation a list of boxes: [[x, y, w, h], [x, y, w, h]] one box: [x, y, w, h], that of the first occurrence (from Trapper's model) camtrapdp=False one row per observation, bboxes is the list one row per observation, bboxes is [x, y, w, h] camtrapdp=True (default) one row per box, each with count 1 one row per observation, with bboxX, bboxY, bboxWidth, bboxHeight

So on v1 an observation of count=2 with two boxes is two rows in the default format, and one in the other. Both are relative coordinates (0 to 1). A box is optional: [] when there is none.

With camtrapdp=False the SDK reads both shapes into row.bboxes, a list of BBox (a v2 observation has one).

A box in the other version's shape breaks the whole results table

The default format (camtrapdp=True) answers 500 for the entire project if one row has its boxes in the other version's shape (a flat box on v1, a list of boxes on v2). I met it writing test data by hand; whether the tools of each version can produce it was not checked. The camtrapdp=False format keeps working.

Two people, one image

The results table has the final classification only, so it never holds two users' observations of the same image. user_classifications lists all of them, each its own record (checked with three users on one image: three records, with their own pk and owner), and approved marks the one the final classification is taken from. When another is approved, the final one copies it (on v1 it replaces the observations, boxes included; the others are left as they were), and the approved mark moves.

Trapper does not match the observations of two classifications (from its source and checked on v1 and v2): there is no link between "the rabbit of ana" and "the rabbit of luis", and the user classification list does not carry the boxes (only bboxes: true; the species, type and count are there), so through the API the boxes of a user's classification cannot be read until it is approved, and then they are in the results table. Its only use of boxes is the task CopyBboxesFromAI, which copies the boxes of an AI classification to the approved expert one when both have the same total count and observation type and the expert's objects are indistinguishable, giving them to the objects at random (its docstring). To tell whether two observations are the same animal, compare their species and count, and, for the approved classification only, its boxes (their overlap).

Not to be confused with the media table

client.classification_media is the table of the project's files; this is what they show. Join them by mediaID: there is an example there.

Reading, then editing

The API cannot create, edit or approve a classification: the list is read-only (Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS on v1 and v2) and the only write is the import. To correct classifications by script: export the results table with camtrapdp=False (the format that carries _id, which the import requires; the default camtrapdp=True does not), edit it and import it.

Endpoints:

  • GET /media_classification/api/classifications (list + detail)
  • GET /media_classification/api/classifications/results/{project_pk}/ — CSV/model export of observations for one project
  • POST /media_classification/api/classifications/import/ — import observations from a CSV

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description project PK The project of the list. Required for deployment and collection: Trapper checks them against the project's own and, without it, answers 400 "Select a valid choice" (which reads as if the deployment did not exist), so the SDK raises a ValueError before the request. The project-scoped methods below take it from the URL owner boolean true = resources where user is owner/manager deployment list of PKs Deployment PKs (needs project) collection list of PKs The pk of the link between the project and the collection, not the collection's pk (needs project; see entry 51 of TRAPPER_API_IMPROVEMENTS.md) locations_map comma-separated PKs Filter by location PKs rdate_from / rdate_to date date_recorded range rtime_from / rtime_to HH:MM Time-of-day range ftype choice Resource type (IMAGE, VIDEO, ...) bboxes boolean Has bounding boxes classified, classified_ai boolean Has a classification by a user / by AI (on v2 the results and media tables answer 500 to these two; the list works) approved boolean Approved. It works on both: Trapper v1 ignores approved and calls the same filter status, so the SDK sends it as status there status boolean Approved, Trapper v1's own name for it (Trapper v2 ignores it, and the SDK warns) species list of PKs Filter by species PKs observation_type choice Filter by observation type sex choice Filter by sex age choice Filter by age

Filters that this endpoint ignores

Trapper ignores a parameter it does not know without an error, and the list comes back unfiltered. Besides the ones above, user, feedback, confidence and ai_provider, which a previous version of this guide listed, do nothing here (checked on v1 and v2: user=1 and ai_provider=1 return every row; they belong to the lists of user and AI classifications). A filter that leaves no row answers 200 with an empty list, but the results table and the media table answer 400 "Empty queryset...", which the SDK reads as an empty result (it is also the answer to a missing permission).

The SDK emits an UnknownFilterWarning that names a parameter the server version does not apply (the request is still sent). Trapper also makes a filter of each custom attribute of the project's classificator, which the SDK cannot know: the warning says so, and warnings.simplefilter("ignore", err.UnknownFilterWarning) silences it.

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
page = client.classification_results.get(page=1, page_size=50, approved=True)
for row in client.classification_results.where(species=42):
    print(row)
result = client.classification_results.get_all(page_size=100)
row = client.classification_results.find(1)

See Usage if any of this looks unfamiliar — it's the same interface on every component.

docs.title: Observation export, scoped to a project
docs.text:
The export endpoint returns a different schema than the one above — CamtrapDP or Trapper-flavoured observation rows (ClassificationRecordExport), depending on what the server returns:

# One page
page = client.classification_results.get_project_results(
    project_pk=7, page=1, page_size=50, approved=True,
)
for row in page.results:
    print(row.observationID, row.scientificName)

# Lazy iteration
for row in client.classification_results.where_project_results(project_pk=7):
    print(row)

# Straight to CSV
client.classification_results.export_project_results(project_pk=7, file="observations.csv")

# Or get model instances instead of a file
records = client.classification_results.export_project_results(project_pk=7, file=None)

Additional field on the export endpoints:

Parameter Type Default Description camtrapdp boolean True True = CamtrapDP standard rows, False = Trapper's internal format

docs.title: Importing observations from a CSV
docs.text:
Unlike locations/deployments import (which simulate an HTML form), this is a real, token-authenticated REST endpoint — the proper way an import should look, and the model the locations/deployments workarounds explicitly fall short of.

result = client.classification_results.import_classifications(
    project_id=7,
    file="observations.csv",
    approve=True,
    import_bboxes=True,
    import_expert_classifications=True,
    import_ai_classifications=False,   # set True + ai_provider_id to import AI rows too
    overwrite_attrs=False,
)
print(result.data.message, result.data.task_id)

If the server runs the import as a Celery task, result.data.task_id is set and the message tells you it's running asynchronously; otherwise the message reflects the synchronous result.

docs.title: Splitting large CSVs
docs.text:
Like import_locations/import_deployments, this accepts split/delay/chunk_size to break a large CSV into several smaller, self-contained chunks (each repeating the header row), uploaded one at a time with a delay between them:

results = client.classification_results.import_classifications(
    project_id=7, file="huge_observations.csv",
    split=True, delay=2,  # <=512 KiB chunks, 2s apart
)
for r in results:
    print(r.data.message, r.data.task_id)

With split=True the return value is a list of results (one per chunk), instead of a single one.

docs.title: Retrying timed-out uploads
docs.text:
If a chunk is still too large/slow for the server, the upload can fail with a network-level timeout rather than a normal error response. retry_attempts/retry_min_wait/retry_max_wait retry that specific failure mode (using tenacity, exponential backoff) — never a 4xx/5xx response, since that's a validation failure a retry can't fix:

client.classification_results.import_classifications(
    project_id=7, file="observations.csv",
    split=True, chunk_size=128 * 1024,  # smaller chunks if the server keeps timing out
    retry_attempts=5, retry_min_wait=2, retry_max_wait=30,
)

Set retry_attempts=1 to disable retrying.

This endpoint doesn't need it the way locations/deployments do

Unlike locations/deployments, this is a real REST endpoint meant to take a full file in one request — only reach for split if a large CSV hits a request-size limit or times out.

This updates existing classifications — it doesn't create new observations

The CSV's _id column must reference classifications that already exist in the target project (the server checks it against a whitelist of that project's classification PKs and rejects anything else). This import re-applies expert/AI classification data (species, count, approval, ...) to those existing rows — it's not a way to add brand-new observations from scratch.

There's also a ready-to-run script: examples/import_classifications.py. It has a --fetch N mode that writes N real existing observation rows from your own project to a CSV (read-only, safe) — since a CSV with made-up _id values will always be rejected, this is the practical way to get something you can actually test with.

docs.title: Classifications Map
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — same code on both. See Trapper versions.

client.classifications_map — resources pending classification for a given project, as used to drive the classification UI's map/queue view.

Endpoint: GET /media_classification/api/classifications_map (list + detail).
