docs.text: Parameter Type Description project PK Filter by classification project PK owner boolean true = resources where user is owner/manager deployment list of PKs Filter by deployment PKs collection list of PKs Filter by collection PKs locations_map comma-separated PKs Filter by location PKs rdate_from / rdate_to date date_recorded range rtime_from / rtime_to HH:MM Time-of-day range ftype choice Resource type (IMAGE, VIDEO, ...) classified boolean Classified by humans classified_ai boolean Classified by AI approved boolean Has a FINAL approved classification species list of PKs Filter by species PKs observation_type choice Filter by observation type

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
This component has no special methods — it's exactly the generic interface described in Usage:

page = client.classifications_map.get(page=1, page_size=50, project=7)
for row in client.classifications_map.where(project=7, classified=False):
    print(row)
result = client.classifications_map.get_all(project=7)
row = client.classifications_map.find(1)
client.classifications_map.export(file="classifications_map.csv")

docs.title: Classificators
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — except create(), which is v1 only. See Trapper versions.

client.classificators — classificator configurations (the taxonomy/attribute schema a classification project classifies against).

Endpoint: GET /media_classification/api/classificators (list + detail).

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description owner boolean true = classificators owned by the user search string Search by name or description

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
This component has no special methods — it's exactly the generic interface described in Usage:

page = client.classificators.get(page=1, page_size=50)
for classificator in client.classificators.where(owner=True):
    print(classificator)
result = client.classificators.get_all()
classificator = client.classificators.find(1)
client.classificators.export(file="classificators.csv")

docs.title: Creating a classificator (Trapper v1)
docs.text:
The REST API is read-only for classificators, so create() works around that by simulating the classic web form media_classification/classificator/create/ via cookie/session auth, like import_locations(). The account that logs in becomes the owner. On Trapper v2 it raises UnsupportedVersionError.

Not a stable API contract

It depends on an unversioned HTML form and needs user_name/user_password (the account's email on servers that log in by email): a token alone cannot authenticate it.

from trapper_client import ClassificatorCreate

lynx = next(iter(client.species.where(search="lynx")))
classificator = client.classificators.create(
    ClassificatorCreate(
        name="Iberian mammals",
        species=[lynx, 5, 6, 7, 8],     # what a classifier can choose from: objects or primary keys
        tracked_species=[lynx],         # the ones Trapper watches
        sex=True,
        age=True,
    )
)
print(classificator.pk, classificator.name)

create() takes a ClassificatorCreate, a Pydantic model, and returns the created classificator. Building the model validates the data before anything is sent. To build it from a dict, use ClassificatorCreate.model_validate(data).

Field Meaning Default name up to 255 characters, unique required template ClassificatorTemplate.INLINE ("inline") or TAB ("tab", tabbed): how the classification form is laid out INLINE species the species a classifier can choose from, as objects from client.species or primary keys. Empty means every species empty tracked_species the species Trapper watches (objects or primary keys): classifying one notifies the administrators of the project (an e-mail and a message). They must be among species when that is not empty empty sex, age, count_new, behaviour, individual_id, classification_confidence add that optional attribute to the classification form False

Observation type, count and "is setup" are always part of the form, so they are not parameters.

species and tracked_species are different lists

species is what a classifier can pick. tracked_species is a subset of those that Trapper keeps an eye on: the same species can be in both, but only the second one raises a notification.

Unknown species are dropped silently

Trapper ignores a species primary key that does not exist: if every key in species is unknown, the classificator is created accepting every species. Check the keys with client.species first when it matters.

Custom and predefined attributes (the extra fields a classificator can add to the form) are not covered. A rejected form raises APIError naming the field, for example name: Classificator with this Name already exists.; raise_on_error=False returns None instead.

docs.title: Collections
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — except the *_ondemand methods, which are v1 only (UnsupportedVersionError on v2). See Trapper versions.

client.collections — storage collections: groups of resources uploaded together.

Endpoints:

  • GET /storage/api/collections (list + detail)
  • GET /storage/api/collections_ondemand — on-demand collections for the current user
  • GET /storage/api/collections_map — collections list for map rendering
  • GET /storage/api/collections_append — collections the user can append resources to
  • POST /storage/api/collection/process/ — trigger processing of an FTP-uploaded collection

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description pk list of PKs Filter by specific collection PKs status choice Private, OnDemand, Public or Archived (CollectionStatus), in any case owner boolean true = only collections owned/managed by current user owners list of PKs Filter by one or more owner user PKs research_projects list of PKs Filter by one or more research project PKs locations_map list of PKs Filter via resources__deployment__location (v1 only: Trapper v2 ignores it) search string Full-text search across name and owner username

Lists (pk, owners, research_projects, locations_map) can be given as a list or as a comma-separated string: pk=[2, 1] and pk="2,1" are the same. Trapper reads pk and locations_map as one string with commas and owners and research_projects as repeated parameters, and pk=[2, 1] sent the other way keeps one pk; the SDK sends each one the way Trapper reads it.

docs.title: Filtering by status
docs.text:
Trapper compares status as it is stored, in upper and lower case, and a value that does not exist is an empty result, not an error: status="private" and status="Bogus" both give no collections. The SDK resolves it with CollectionStatus (Private, OnDemand, Public, Archived), accepting any case, the label ("On demand") or the member, and raises a ValueError listing the valid ones before any request when it is none of them:

from trapper_client import CollectionStatus

client.collections.where(status="public")                    # the same as "Public"
client.collections.where(status=CollectionStatus.ON_DEMAND)
client.collections.where(status="Bogus")                     # ValueError: use one of Private, OnDemand, Public, Archived

A filter that Trapper does not apply

Trapper ignores a parameter that is not one of its filters without an error, and the list comes back unfiltered; the SDK emits an UnknownFilterWarning that names it (the request is still sent). Besides those in the table, the list applies name, period_begin, period_end, is_complete_cs_collection, cs_deployment, managers and members. locations_map is ignored by v2, and description, date_created and ordering by both. To silence it: warnings.simplefilter("ignore", err.UnknownFilterWarning).

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
# Lazy iteration (all() is the same thing)
for col in client.collections.where():
    print(col)
for col in client.collections.where(owner=True):
    print(col)
for col in client.collections.where(research_projects=3):
    print(col)

# One page
page = client.collections.get(page=1, page_size=25)
print(page.pagination.count)

# Single item
col = client.collections.find(42)

See Usage if any of this looks unfamiliar — it's the same interface on every component.

Resources inside a collection

CollectionsComponent only lists collections themselves — for the resources inside one, use client.resources.where_by_collection(collection_pk=...).

docs.title: On-demand / map / append sub-endpoints
docs.text:
Three related endpoints get the exact same where_*/get_*/get_all_*/find_* set as the main one, just scoped to a different collection subset:

# On-demand collections for the current user
for col in client.collections.where_ondemand():
    print(col)
page = client.collections.get_ondemand(page_size=25)
result = client.collections.get_all_ondemand()
col = client.collections.find_ondemand(42)

# Collections for map rendering
for col in client.collections.where_map():
    print(col)

# Collections the user can append resources to
for col in client.collections.where_append():
    print(col)

What each one gives (checked on Trapper v1 and v2):

Method Fields Pagination v2 main (where(), get(), ...) the nine of Collection paginated yes *_ondemand the same nine paginated no: UnsupportedVersionError (Trapper answers 404) *_map the same nine none: Trapper returns one plain list and ignores page_size yes *_append only pk and name (the other fields are None) none: one plain list yes

The SDK wraps a plain list as a single page, so get_map() and get_all_append() work like the others and pagination.count is the length of the list. delete_data, update_data, detail_data and owner_profile are web page URLs on v1 and None on v2.

docs.title: Creating a collection from a package
docs.text:
A collection with its resources is created from a package: a ZIP with the files and a YAML that describes them. The SDK has the two steps, and nothing else creates a collection with data: get_uploader() puts the two files in the account's collections/ folder on the server, and trigger_collection() makes Trapper process them.

from pathlib import Path

uploader = client.get_uploader()                       # chunked on v1, resumable (tus) on v2
uploader.upload(Path("package.yaml"), "collections/package.yaml")
uploader.upload(Path("package.zip"), "collections/package.zip")

response = client.collections.trigger_collection({"yaml_file": "package.yaml", "zip_file": "package.zip"})
print(response.json()["data"]["task_id"])              # the task has started: the collection is not there yet

# wait for it: the collection and its resources appear a few seconds later
import time
while not (found := list(client.collections.where(search="My collection"))):
    time.sleep(3)

The YAML (Trapper validates it against collection_schema.yaml; a problem is a BadRequestError with the details in data.errors):

collections:
  - name: My collection              # reused if the account already has one with this name (in Trapper's code)
    resources_dir: res               # the folder of the ZIP that holds one folder per deployment
    project_id: 3                    # a CLASSIFICATION project (the research project comes from it)
    timezone: Europe/Madrid          # must be the one of the deployments' locations
    timezone_ignore_dst: false       # and so must this
    managers:                        # optional
      - username: ana
    deployments:
      - deployment_id: don01-2024a   # an existing deployment of the project's research project
        resources:
          - name: don01-2024a_0001
            file: IMG_0001.JPG       # res/don01-2024a/IMG_0001.JPG in the ZIP
            date_recorded: '2024-03-01T10:00:00+01:00'
            mime_type: image/jpeg    # optional, like file_width, file_height, file_size, file_fps, file_duration

and the ZIP has res/don01-2024a/IMG_0001.JPG, that is <resources_dir>/<deployment_id>/<file>.

What it needs (checked on Trapper v1 and v2, except what says in Trapper's code):

  • The classification project and the deployments must exist and the account must be able to upload to the project. The SDK creates deployments by import, and classification projects on v1 only (client.classification_projects.create()).
  • The timezone and timezone_ignore_dst of the YAML must match the deployments' locations, or Trapper refuses it.
  • The account needs uploader access (on v2 an HTTP uploader account, see versions), and on v1 the uploader is served by Trapper's nginx: a development server on its own port answers 404 to the login.
  • In Trapper's code: a file that is identical (same content) to one already in the deployment, or that has an extension Trapper does not accept, is skipped and written to a .log file next to the ZIP, without failing the rest.
  • On v2 the uploaded files can take a moment to be in place: if trigger_collection() answers NotFoundError ("not found in your upload directory") right after the upload, wait a couple of seconds and call it again.
  • trigger_ai_pipeline is True by default, and starts the AI detection on the new resources; pass False to skip it.
  • In Trapper's code: the thumbnails and previews are built after the resources exist, so resources.download(pk, ..., kind="thumbnail") may answer NotFoundError for a moment. Once built, they download (checked on v1).

docs.title: Downloading the files of a collection
docs.text: client.collections.download_resources(pk, "downloads/") saves the files of a collection into downloads/<collection name>/, with the filters of the resource list to choose which ones, skipping what is already there. See Downloading all the files of a deployment or a collection.

docs.title: Triggering FTP-uploaded collection processing
docs.text:
trigger_collection() starts the processing of a data package (a YAML definition and a ZIP) that is already in the account's own folder on the server: it does not upload anything (see the uploader for that).

response = client.collections.trigger_collection(
    payload={
        "yaml_file": "package_123.yaml",
        "zip_file": "package_123.zip",
        "remove_zip": False,
    },
)
print(response.json()["data"]["task_id"])

yaml_file and zip_file are required; remove_zip (default False), extract_metadata (default False) and trigger_ai_pipeline (default True) are optional. Trapper checks the YAML definition and starts a background task (it runs in the request itself only if the server has Celery off), so a 200 means it was started, not that the collection exists. The answer is {"data": {"message": ..., "errors": ..., "task_id": ...}}. A missing name or an invalid YAML is a BadRequestError (the problems are in data.errors), and a file that is not in the account's folder is a NotFoundError; with raise_on_error=False the raw response is returned instead.

docs.title: Deployments
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — import_deployments() works on both but behaves differently (see below), and geojson() is v2 only. See Trapper versions.

client.deployments — camera deployments at a location, over a time range.

Endpoints: GET /geomap/api/deployments (list + detail), GET /geomap/api/deployments/export/ (CSV export).

The REST API is otherwise read-only for this resource; see Importing deployments below for the one write operation this component supports.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description location int or list Filter by location ID(s) research_project int or list Filter by research project ID(s) tags int or list Filter by tag ID(s) owner bool Filter by current user ownership sdate_from, sdate_to date (ISO) Filter by start date range edate_from, edate_to date (ISO) Filter by end date range classification_project int Filter by classification project ID correct_setup bool Filter by setup correctness correct_tstamp bool Filter by timestamp correctness search str Search in deployment_id or owner username

Trapper ignores a filter it does not know

A parameter that is not a filter of Trapper (a typo, colls, ordering, radius...) is ignored without an error, and the list comes back unfiltered. The SDK knows the filters of each Trapper version and, when you pass another one, emits an UnknownFilterWarning that names it (the request is still sent). Besides those in the table, the list applies pk, deployment_code, deployment_id, setup_by, camera_*, detection_distance, bait_type, feature_type, habitat, session, array, comments, date_created, managers, start_date, end_date, is_incomplete, view_quality, capture_method and status, and v2 also applies in_bbox. To silence it: warnings.simplefilter("ignore", err.UnknownFilterWarning).

docs.title: Filtering by area
docs.text:
A deployment has no coordinates of its own: they are its location's, and the deployment list gives only the location's pk, so where() has no spatial filter. in_area() takes the same area as client.locations.in_area() and returns the deployments whose location is inside:

# a bounding box: (min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat)
for dep in client.deployments.in_area(bbox=(-7.0, 36.5, -5.5, 37.5)):
    print(dep.deployment_id, dep.location_id)

# a circle: the centre as (longitude, latitude), the radius in metres, plus the usual filters
near = list(client.deployments.in_area(center=(-6.44, 37.05), radius=5_000, research_project=3, sdate_from="2024-01-01"))

It finds the locations in the area first (every location the account can see is read and filtered on the client) and then asks for the deployments of those locations, 50 location pks per request. The other keywords are filters of the deployments, not of the locations, and location cannot be combined with the area. A deployment whose location has no readable coordinates is left out, and a wrong area raises ValueError before any request for deployments.

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
# One page
page = client.deployments.get(page=1, page_size=25, research_project=3)

# Every page merged
result = client.deployments.get_all(page_size=100)

# Lazy iteration (all() is the same thing)
for dep in client.deployments.where(location=42, sdate_from="2024-01-01"):
    print(dep)
for dep in client.deployments.all():
    print(dep)

# Single item
dep = client.deployments.find(99)

# CSV export
client.deployments.export(file="deployments.csv")

See Usage if any of this looks unfamiliar — it's the same interface on every component.

There is no collection filter: Trapper's deployment API has none, and it silently ignores any parameter it doesn't know (such as colls), returning every deployment instead. Use the shortcut below.

docs.title: Shortcut: by collection
docs.text:
by_collection() returns the deployments with at least one resource in a collection. The deployment API can't filter by collection, but the resource API can filter by collection and deployment at once: every candidate deployment — whatever where() returns for the filters you pass — is checked with one single-item resource request, max_workers (8 by default) in parallel. Narrow the candidates, usually with research_project: with no filter, every deployment on the server is checked.

# Deployments of research project 3 with images in collection 5
for dep in client.deployments.by_collection(5, research_project=3):
    print(dep)

# ...with how many images each one has there
for dep, count in client.deployments.by_collection_with_counts(5, research_project=3):
    print(dep.deployment_id, count)

# Export them to CSV
client.deployments.export_by_collection(5, research_project=3, file="deps.csv")

collection_id is the storage collection's own pk — collection_pk in a classification project's collection list (classification_projects.get_all_project_collections()).

docs.title: GeoJSON (Trapper v2 only)
docs.text:
geojson() returns the deployments as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection. It replaces client.maps and client.locations_geojson, which Trapper v2 removed; on a v1 server it raises UnsupportedVersionError.

fc = client.deployments.geojson(classification_project=2, species=[3, 7])
for feature in fc["features"]:
    lon, lat = feature["geometry"]["coordinates"]
    print(feature["properties"]["deploymentID"], lon, lat)
Parameter Description classification_project Keep deployments linked to this classification project; scopes observation_type and species to its classifications observation_type One value or a list ("animal", ["animal", "human"]) species One species pk or a list start_date_gte, end_date_lte Deployments starting on/after, or ending on/before, a date (YYYY-MM-DD) refresh Bypass the server's one-hour cache for this query

Only deployments the current user can access are returned.

docs.title: Downloading the files
docs.text: client.deployments.download_resources(pk, "downloads/") saves the images or videos of a deployment into downloads/<deployment_id>/, with the filters of the resource list to choose which ones, skipping what is already there. See Downloading all the files of a deployment or a collection.

docs.title: Fields: the list and the export
docs.text:
Like locations, a deployment comes in two shapes, and neither holds every field. where(), get() and find() return a Deployment (Trapper's JSON): pk, deployment_code, deployment_id, location (the location's pk), location_id, start_date, end_date, owner, research_project (its acronym), tags, correct_setup and correct_tstamp. export(file=None) returns a DeploymentExport for each row of the CSV, which has the camera and setup fields instead (setup_by, camera_*, detection_distance, bait_use, feature_type, habitat, session, array, comments, longitude, latitude, location_name) but not the owner, the research project or correct_setup and correct_tstamp. Both have pk, deployment_id, location_id, start_date, end_date and tags. Checked on Trapper v1 and v2.

start_date and end_date are timezone-aware datetime objects in both shapes, although Trapper spells them differently (2024-01-01T00:00:00+01:00 in the JSON, 2024-01-01T00:00:00+0100 in the CSV), so they can be compared and sorted whichever you read. A date that cannot be read is kept as the text it came as, and an empty one is None. export(file="x.csv") writes them back as ISO text with the colon (+01:00); raw=True keeps Trapper's own spelling.

Trapper's CSV has no column for session, array, tags or bait_type: it puts the first two in deploymentGroups (session:S | array:A) and the tags in deploymentTags, with baitType:<value> added when the deployment has a bait type. DeploymentExport reads them from there, so tags holds only the tags and bait_type the bait. To get the CSV exactly as Trapper sends it, use export(file=..., raw=True).

To read the camera of a deployment, or its habitat, use the export; to read its owner, its research project or correct_setup, use the list. When you need both, join them by pk, giving the export the same filters as the list so that both return the same deployments:

filters = {"research_project": 3}
by_pk = {row.pk: row for row in client.deployments.export(query=filters, file=None)}

for dep in client.deployments.where(**filters):
    row = by_pk.get(dep.pk)
    print(dep.deployment_id, dep.owner, row.camera_height, row.habitat, row.session)

Run against Trapper v1 and v2, every deployment of the list was in the export. If no deployment matches the filters, the export raises BadRequestError ("Empty queryset"), because Trapper answers an empty export with a 400; the list gives an empty result. A few fields of a deployment are in neither shape, so they cannot be read through the API: view_quality, date_created, managers, capture_method, is_incomplete and status (taken from Trapper's model, not checked on a server).

docs.title: Importing deployments (write access)
docs.text:
/geomap/api/deployments is read-only, so import_deployments() works around that by simulating the classic web UI's geomap/deployment/import/ form via cookie/session auth instead of the API's token auth (see APIClientBase.session_login).

On Trapper v2 the same method posts to the import action of the Django admin (admin/geomap/deployment/import-deployments/). The account must be a staff user with the add permission, and the server imports asynchronously: True means the table passed validation and was queued, so poll client.deployments if you need the rows to be there. Rejected tables raise APIError with the server's message and the per-row errors.

Not a stable API contract

Same caveat as locations import: this depends on an unversioned HTML form and requires user_name/user_password (account email). See the method's docstring for the full warning.

Unlike locations, timezone is required here — the server form has no default. research_project is also required (same reason as for locations: the field is declared required=False but its clean_research_project() rejects a missing value):

client.deployments.import_deployments(
    file="deployments.csv",
    timezone="Europe/Madrid",           # required
    research_project=7,                 # required
    classification_project=3,           # optional, links all imported deployments to it
    create_locations=True,              # requires locationID/longitude/latitude columns in the CSV
    update=False,                       # True updates existing deployments (requires an _id column)
)

There's also a ready-to-run script: examples/import_deployments.py.

docs.title: Waiting for the import to land
docs.text:
On Trapper v2 the import runs in the background: import_deployments() returning True means the table was validated and queued, not that the rows exist yet. Neither version exposes the import task through the API, so wait_for_import() checks the outcome instead — it polls until every deploymentID is listed:

client.deployments.import_deployments(file="deployments.csv", research_project=1, timezone="Europe/Madrid")
client.deployments.wait_for_import(["DON01-2024A", "DON01-2024B"], timeout=60)   # raises TimeoutError if missing

Pass raise_on_timeout=False to get False back instead. It works the same on v1.

docs.title: Updating deployments
docs.text:
Trapper has no endpoint to edit a deployment, but the import updates the ones that exist when it gets update=True and an _id column with their primary keys. The CSV that Trapper exports has that column, so the way to correct deployments is export, edit, import:

import csv

# 1. Export the deployments exactly as Trapper sends them (raw=True keeps the _id column and the header)
path = client.deployments.export(file="deployments.csv", raw=True, research_project=7)

# 2. Edit the CSV: change the cells you want, keep the header and the _id
with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
for row in rows:
    if row["deploymentID"] == "don01-2024a":
        row["cameraHeight"] = "1.25"
        row["habitat"] = "dehesa"
with open("edited.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(rows)

# 3. Import it with update=True, and wait until the new values are there
client.deployments.import_deployments(
    file="edited.csv", research_project=7, timezone="Europe/Madrid", update=True,
)
client.deployments.wait_for_update({"don01-2024a": {"camera_height": 1.25, "habitat": "dehesa"}})

import_deployments() returns True when the table is validated and queued, on v1 and v2: the changes are applied a moment later. wait_for_import() cannot tell, because the IDs exist already, so wait_for_update() polls the export until each deployment has the values you give, with the field names of DeploymentExport (numbers are compared with a tolerance). It raises TimeoutError, or returns False with raise_on_timeout=False, if they do not arrive in timeout seconds. Give it the stored ID: Trapper slugifies the deploymentID of an import ("Don 01" is stored as "don-01"). Checked on Trapper v1 and v2. As on the rest of the imports, the account must be staff on v2.

docs.title: What you get in the exception when the CSV itself is rejected
docs.text:
Same as locations: if the CSV fails the server's table validation (wrong/missing columns, a deploymentID/locationID that already exists, ...), the raised err.APIError includes the actual per-row messages parsed out of the server's embedded validation report, e.g.:

Deployment import failed (status 200): locationID 'dona-001' already exists

docs.title: Uploading a very large CSV: split
docs.text:
Same mechanism as locations: there's no chunked/resumable upload protocol on this endpoint, so split=True breaks the CSV into several smaller, self-contained chunks (each repeating the header row) and imports them one request at a time, sleeping delay seconds (default 1) between uploads:

client.deployments.import_deployments(
    file="huge_deployments.csv",
    timezone="Europe/Madrid",
    research_project=7,
    split=True,
    delay=2,
    chunk_size=512 * 1024,  # bytes per chunk — this is also the default
)

split + create_locations=True

Each chunk is imported as an independent request, so if the same locationID appears in more than one chunk, the server will try to create that location again in every chunk that references it — it has no memory of locations created by a previous chunk. Only combine split with create_locations=True if you know each locationID falls within a single chunk, or pre-create the locations separately and import with create_locations=False instead.

With raise_on_error=True (the default), the whole call raises as soon as one chunk fails, without uploading the rest; with raise_on_error=False it uploads every chunk regardless and returns False if any of them failed.

docs.title: Retrying a chunk that times out: retry_attempts
docs.text: Same mechanism as locations: a network-level timeout on an oversized/slow chunk is retried automatically (tenacity, exponential backoff) via retry_attempts/retry_min_wait/retry_max_wait — never an HTTP error response, which is a validation failure a retry can't fix. Set retry_attempts=1 to disable retrying.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — import_locations() works on both but behaves differently (see below). See Trapper versions.

client.locations — read/write access to camera-trap locations.

Endpoint: GET /geomap/api/locations (list + detail), GET /geomap/api/locations/export/ (CSV export).

The REST API is otherwise read-only for this resource; see Importing locations below for the one write operation this component supports.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description name string Partial, case-insensitive match on location name description string Partial, case-insensitive match on description owner boolean true = only locations owned by the current user owners list of PKs Filter by one or more owner user PKs research_project list of PKs Filter by one or more research projects locations_map list of PKs Filter by locations associated to a map deployments list of PKs Filter locations that have those deployments search string Global text search across location_id, name, description, county, city, owner username

Trapper ignores a filter it does not know

A parameter that is not in this table, or that a typo turned into another name, is ignored without an error, and the list comes back unfiltered. The SDK knows the filters of each Trapper version and, when you pass another one, emits an UnknownFilterWarning that names it (the request is still sent). Besides those in the table, the list applies pk, location_id, is_public, ignore_DST, coordinate_uncertainty, date_created, managers and research_projects_member on both versions, and country, state, county and city on v1 only (locations_map also on v1 only). in_bbox is applied by v2 only; radius and ordering by neither. To silence it: warnings.simplefilter("ignore", err.UnknownFilterWarning).

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
# One page
page = client.locations.get(page=1, page_size=25)

# Every page merged
result = client.locations.get_all(page_size=100)

# Lazy iteration (all() is the same thing, use whichever reads better)
for loc in client.locations.where(research_project=1):
    print(loc)
for loc in client.locations.all():
    print(loc)

# By owner and free text
for loc in client.locations.where(owner=True, search="camera"):
    print(loc)

# Single item
loc = client.locations.find(42)

# CSV export (also accepts filters)
client.locations.export(file="locations.csv")
client.locations.export(query={"research_project": 5}, file="project5_locations.csv")

See Usage if any of this looks unfamiliar — it's the same interface on every component.

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text:
Trapper returns the coordinates of a location as one string, with the longitude first ("-6.44, 37.05"), in v1 and v2. Location.coordinates keeps it as it comes, and longitude and latitude give it as numbers:

loc = client.locations.find(16)
loc.coordinates         # "-6.44, 37.05"
loc.longitude           # -6.44
loc.latitude            # 37.05

They are None when the coordinates are missing, cannot be read or are out of range (longitude beyond ±180, latitude beyond ±90): one odd location does not break a listing. They are read from coordinates each time, not fields of the model, so model_dump() does not change. The rows of export(file=None) carry longitude and latitude already.

docs.title: Filtering by area
docs.text:
Trapper's location list has no usable spatial filter. Trapper v1 ignores in_bbox and radius without an error and returns every location (the GeoJSON endpoint applies them, but only on v1); v2 applies in_bbox but ignores radius. in_area() filters on the client instead, with the coordinates as numbers, so it works the same on both:

# a bounding box: (min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat)
for loc in client.locations.in_area(bbox=(-7.0, 36.5, -5.5, 37.5)):
    print(loc.name, loc.longitude, loc.latitude)

# a circle: the centre as (longitude, latitude), the radius in metres, plus the usual filters
near = list(client.locations.in_area(center=(-6.44, 37.05), radius=5_000, research_project=3))

Give a box, a circle or both (a location must then be inside both). The edges of the box are inside, a box with min_lon greater than max_lon crosses the antimeridian (±180°), and the distances are great-circle (haversine) ones. Any other keyword is an ordinary filter of the list, sent to the server, so it narrows down what has to be read. A wrong area (nothing given, center without radius, out of range) raises ValueError before any request.

It reads every page

The server cannot do all the filtering, so in_area() reads the locations that match the other filters and keeps the ones in the area. On v2 a box is also sent to the server (in_bbox), and only the locations in it are read, unless it crosses the antimeridian; on v1, and for a circle alone, every page is read. On a server with many locations, pass research_project or owner. A location whose coordinates cannot be read is left out.

docs.title: Fields: the list and the export
docs.text:
Trapper gives a location in two shapes, and neither holds every field. where(), get() and find() return a Location, built from Trapper's JSON; export(file=None) returns a LocationExport for each row of its CSV. Checked on Trapper v1 and v2:

Field Location (find(), get(), where()) LocationExport (export(file=None)) pk, location_id, description, timezone yes yes name, owner, owner_profile, is_public, date_created yes no city, county, state yes (not on v2) no country yes (not on v2) yes Coordinates coordinates, a string, and longitude and latitude read from it longitude and latitude Research project research_project, its acronym research_project_id, its primary key ignore_dst no yes habitat no yes coordinate_uncertainty, managers no no

To save the export as Trapper sends it, with its own header (locationID, ignoreDST, _id, researchProject, ...) instead of the SDK's column names, use client.locations.export(file="locations.csv", raw=True).

So to read the ignore_dst of a location, or the primary key of its research project, use the export; to read its name or its owner, use the list. coordinate_uncertainty and managers exist in Trapper but are in neither, and cannot be read. When you need both, join them by pk; give the export the same filters as the list so that both return the same locations:

filters = {"research_project": 3}
by_pk = {row.pk: row for row in client.locations.export(query=filters, file=None)}

for loc in client.locations.where(**filters):
    row = by_pk.get(loc.pk)
    print(loc.name, loc.longitude, row.ignore_dst, row.research_project_id)

Trapper builds each shape from its own serializer, with its own list of fields, which is why they differ (entry 23 of TRAPPER_API_IMPROVEMENTS.md).

docs.title: Importing locations (write access)
docs.text:
/geomap/api/locations is read-only, so import_locations() works around that by simulating the classic web UI's geomap/location/import/ form via cookie/session auth instead of the API's token auth (see APIClientBase.session_login).

On Trapper v2 the same method posts to the import action of the Django admin (admin/geomap/location/import-locations/). The account must be a staff user with the add permission, and the server imports asynchronously: True means the table passed validation and was queued. Rejected tables raise APIError with the server's message and the per-row errors.

Not a stable API contract

This depends on an unversioned HTML form, not a documented endpoint — a Trapper change to that page can break it silently. It requires user_name/user_password (the account's email address on servers with ACCOUNT_LOGIN_METHODS = {"email"}) — a token alone cannot authenticate it. See the full caveat in the method's docstring before relying on it.

client.locations.import_locations(
    file="locations.csv",
    research_project=7,       # required — see note below
    timezone="Europe/Madrid", # required — see note below
)

research_project and timezone are required, despite the server's fields saying otherwise

The server's LocationImportForm declares both fields required=False, but:

  • clean_research_project() rejects a missing value with "You have to select a research project." — a 200 (re-rendered form) that's easy to mistake for success if you only check the status code.
  • timezone is worse: nothing rejects a blank value at import time. The server persists locations via Location.objects.bulk_create(), which skips normal model validation — so a blank/omitted timezone silently creates locations with a corrupt timezone value. Nothing fails until later, when something lists or filters those locations (this API, or the classic web UI's own location list) and the serializer trips over the bad value — typically a 500 on an otherwise-unrelated request, long after the import reported success. This method requires timezone up front specifically to prevent creating that kind of latent, hard-to-diagnose corruption.

docs.title: Waiting for the import to land
docs.text:
On Trapper v2 the import runs in the background: import_locations() returning True means the table was validated and queued, not that the rows exist yet. Neither version exposes the import task through the API, so wait_for_import() checks the outcome instead — it polls until every locationID is listed:

client.locations.import_locations(file="locations.csv", research_project=1, timezone="Europe/Madrid")
client.locations.wait_for_import(["don-01", "don-02"], timeout=60)   # raises TimeoutError if missing

Pass raise_on_timeout=False to get False back instead. It works the same on v1.

There's also a ready-to-run script: examples/import_locations.py.

docs.title: What you get in the exception when the CSV itself is rejected
docs.text:
If the CSV fails the server's table validation (wrong/missing columns, a locationID that already exists in this research project, ...), the raised err.APIError includes the actual per-row messages, not just the generic banner — e.g.:

Location import failed (status 200): locationID 'dona-001' already exists; longitude must be a number

The server renders those details as a JSON blob for a JS widget, not as plain HTML text — see APIClientBase._extract_html_error_text for how this is parsed out.

docs.title: Uploading a very large CSV: split
docs.text:
There's no chunked/resumable upload protocol on this endpoint — unlike the HTTPUploader component (a separate, true chunked uploader for a different endpoint), it's a plain single-request form POST. If a large CSV gets rejected or times out, pass split=True to break it into several smaller, self-contained CSV chunks (each repeating the header row) and import them one request at a time:

client.locations.import_locations(
    file="huge_locations.csv",
    research_project=7,
    timezone="Europe/Madrid",
    split=True,
    delay=2,        # seconds between chunk uploads — defaults to 1
    chunk_size=512 * 1024,  # bytes per chunk — this is also the default
)

split is not compatible with gpx_file (raises ValueError) — splitting only makes sense for the CSV path, and the server rejects a request carrying both file types anyway. With raise_on_error=True (the default), the whole call raises as soon as one chunk fails, without uploading the rest; with raise_on_error=False it uploads every chunk regardless and returns False if any of them failed.

docs.title: Retrying a chunk that times out: retry_attempts
docs.text:
If a chunk is still too large/slow for the server, the request itself can fail with a network-level timeout (rather than a normal error response) before the server even gets to respond. That's retried automatically — using tenacity, with exponential backoff — up to retry_attempts times:

client.locations.import_locations(
    file="huge_locations.csv",
    research_project=7,
    timezone="Europe/Madrid",
    split=True,
    chunk_size=128 * 1024,  # try smaller chunks if the server keeps timing out
    retry_attempts=5,       # default is 3
    retry_min_wait=2,       # seconds, default 1
    retry_max_wait=30,      # seconds, default 10
)

Only network-level failures (timeouts, connection resets, ...) are retried — never an HTTP error response (a 4xx/5xx from the server is a validation failure, not something a retry fixes). Set retry_attempts=1 to disable retrying.

docs.title: Related: locations as GeoJSON
docs.text: For map rendering, use client.locations_geojson instead — a different endpoint returning a single GeoJSON FeatureCollection, with its own filter set (bounding box, radius, ...).

docs.title: Locations GeoJSON
docs.text:
Trapper v1 only

Removed in Trapper v2: on a v2 server this raises UnsupportedVersionError. See Trapper versions.

client.locations_geojson — locations as a single GeoJSON FeatureCollection, for map rendering.

Endpoint: GET /geomap/api/locations/geojson/.

docs.title: This component only supports get()
docs.text:
Unlike every other component, this endpoint returns one GeoJSON document — not a paginated list — so get_all(), where(), all(), find(), and export() all raise NotImplementedError. Use get() directly:

geojson = client.locations_geojson.get()
print(geojson["type"])           # "FeatureCollection"
print(len(geojson["features"]))  # number of locations

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
In addition to the locations filters, this endpoint adds:

Parameter Type Description locations Location PKs Alias for locations_map colls Collection PKs Filter by collections associated via deployments reses Resource PKs Filter by resources associated via deployments classes Classification PKs Filter by classifications associated via deployments radius lon,lat,meters Filter by distance from a point search string Searches location_id, name, description, county, city, owner username, deployments__deployment_id in_bbox minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat Filter locations within a geographic bounding box

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Filter by collection ID
geojson = client.locations_geojson.get(collection_id=3)

# Filter by research project
geojson = client.locations_geojson.get(research_project=5)

# Text search
geojson = client.locations_geojson.get(search="camera trap")

# Bounding box (minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat)
geojson = client.locations_geojson.get(in_bbox="-6.0,36.0,0.0,44.0")

# Radius (lon, lat, meters)
geojson = client.locations_geojson.get(radius="-5.5,37.3,10000")

# Combine filters
geojson = client.locations_geojson.get(
    research_project=2,
    search="river",
    in_bbox="-6.0,36.0,0.0,44.0",
)

# Access feature properties
geojson = client.locations_geojson.get(owner=True)
for feature in geojson["features"]:
    props = feature["properties"]
    coords = feature["geometry"]["coordinates"]
    print(f"{props['name']} → lon={coords[0]}, lat={coords[1]}")

docs.title: Maps
docs.text:
Trapper v1 only

Removed in Trapper v2: on a v2 server this raises UnsupportedVersionError. See Trapper versions.

client.maps — umap-based maps accessible to the current user.

Endpoint: GET /geomap/api/maps (list + detail).

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description owner boolean true = maps owned by the current user search string Free-text search across name, description, owner username

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
This component has no special methods — it's exactly the generic interface described in Usage:

page = client.maps.get(page=1, page_size=50)
for m in client.maps.where(owner=True):
    print(m)
result = client.maps.get_all()
m = client.maps.find(1)
client.maps.export(file="maps.csv")

docs.title: Project deployments (Trapper v2)
docs.text:
Trapper v2 serves the deployments of a classification project under api/deployments/<slug>/, together with the actions on them. The SDK wraps it as client.project_deployments; on a v1 server every method raises UnsupportedVersionError.

<slug> is the project's slug, and the project must be a Citizen Science one (public or private) with a classificator; any other slug answers 404. All methods take the slug first.

slug = "mamiferos-donana-sm"

for dep in client.project_deployments.where(slug):
    print(dep.deployment_id, dep.location_name, [s.latin_name for s in dep.species])

client.project_deployments.locations(slug)             # locations with their deployment count
dep = client.project_deployments.find(slug, 3)         # the full, editable record

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
Method Returns get(slug, page=, page_size=, **filters) PaginatedResult[ProjectDeployment] where(slug, **filters) lazy APIQuery[ProjectDeployment] locations(slug) list[ProjectLocation] find(slug, pk) ProjectDeploymentDetail progress(slug, pk) ProjectDeploymentProgress (running, stages) — AI pipeline progress calibration_results(slug, pk) raw rows; empty until a calibration ran

The listing only contains the deployments you may see: the ones you own or manage, public ones, those shared through a team, and all of them if your role in the project can view classifications.

docs.title: Changing a deployment
docs.text:
client.project_deployments.update(slug, 3, comments="Camera moved 2 m north")   # PATCH
client.project_deployments.update_timestamps(slug, 3, time_offset=-3600)        # clock was 1 h ahead
client.project_deployments.delete(slug, 3)                                       # irreversible
  • update() needs can_update; delete() needs can_delete (both are flags on each row).
  • Trapper rewrites deployment_id when it saves a deployment (it appends the location code, e.g. don01-2024a → don01-2024a-don-01), whichever field you change.
  • update_timestamps() shifts the recorded date of every resource of the deployment by time_offset seconds; the classifications' dates are synchronised by a background task.

docs.title: AI calibration
docs.text: request_depth_calibration() and request_distance_estimation() start jobs on the project's AI models and answer 400 when the project has none configured. They are wrapped from Trapper's source, but have only been exercised against mocks: the test servers have no AI deployed.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: For deployments in bulk (import, export, GeoJSON) see Deployments.

docs.title: Research Projects
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — except create(), which is v1 only. See Trapper versions.

client.research_projects — top-level research projects; every collection and classification project belongs to exactly one.

Endpoints:

  • GET /research/api/projects (list + detail)
  • GET /research/api/project/{project_pk}/collections (collections linked to a project)

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description owner bool Only projects owned/managed by the current user keywords repeated int Filter by keyword IDs acronym str Exact acronym filter search str Text search in name, acronym, abstract, owner username no-pagination any value Disables pagination server-side

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
# One page
page = client.research_projects.get(page=1, page_size=50)
print(page.pagination, len(page.results))

# Lazy iteration (all() is the same thing)
for proj in client.research_projects.where(owner=True, acronym="WINTEL"):
    print(proj)
for proj in client.research_projects.where(search="Donana"):
    print(proj)

# CSV export
client.research_projects.export(file="research_projects.csv")

See Usage if any of this looks unfamiliar — it's the same interface on every component.

docs.title: Collections linked to a project
docs.text:
Every access pattern has a _project_collections counterpart, scoped to /research/api/project/{project_pk}/collections:

# One page
cols = client.research_projects.get_project_collections(project_pk=7)
print(cols.pagination, len(cols.results))

# Lazy iteration
for col in client.research_projects.where_project_collections(project_pk=7):
    print(col)

# Every page merged
result = client.research_projects.get_all_project_collections(project_pk=7)

# Single linked collection
col = client.research_projects.find_project_collection(project_pk=7, pk=12)

pk here is a link pk, not the storage collection pk

find_project_collection's pk is the primary key of the ResearchProjectCollection row that links this project to a collection — not the storage Collection's own pk. Passing the storage collection's pk instead will either 404 or return the wrong row.

How to get the right pk:

  • If you only know the project and the storage collection pk, resolve it with find_collection_in_project(project_pk, collection_pk) below — it returns the matching link pk, or None if that collection isn't linked to the project.
  • If you're already iterating get_project_collections()/where_project_collections(), each item's own .pk is the link pk you need — no extra lookup required.

Check whether a specific storage collection is linked to a project, without knowing the link pk:

link_pk = client.research_projects.find_collection_in_project(
    project_pk=7,
    collection_pk=42,
)
if link_pk:
    print(f"Collection 42 is linked via pk={link_pk}")
else:
    print("Collection 42 is not in this project")

These are thin wrappers around a nested component, client.research_projects.collections (an instance of ResearchProjectsCollectionsComponent), which you can also use directly if you prefer:

for col in client.research_projects.collections.where_project(project_pk=7):
    print(col)

docs.title: Creating a research project (Trapper v1)
docs.text:
The REST API is read-only for research projects, so create() works around that by simulating the classic web form research/project/create/ via cookie/session auth, like import_locations(). The account that logs in becomes the project's owner and administrator. On Trapper v2 it raises UnsupportedVersionError.

Not a stable API contract

It depends on an unversioned HTML form and needs user_name/user_password (the account's email on servers that log in by email) — a token alone cannot authenticate it.

from trapper_client import BaitUse, ResearchProjectCreate, SamplingDesign

project = client.research_projects.create(
    ResearchProjectCreate(
        name="Doñana mammals",
        acronym="DONMAM",                       # 3 to 10 characters; name and acronym are unique
        sampling_design=SamplingDesign.TARGETED,
        bait_use=BaitUse.SCENT,
        keywords=["camera trap", "mammals"],
        abstract="Medium and large mammals of Doñana National Park.",
    )
)
print(project.pk, project.name)

create() takes a ResearchProjectCreate, a Pydantic model with every field of the creation form. Building it validates the data before anything is sent: it trims the text, rejects unknown fields (a typo fails instead of being ignored) and raises pydantic.ValidationError, a ValueError, naming the field that is wrong. To build it from a dict (a JSON or YAML file, say), use ResearchProjectCreate.model_validate(data).

Field Values Default name up to 255 characters, unique required acronym 3 to 10 characters, unique required sampling_design SamplingDesign: simpleRandom (1), systematicRandom (2), clusteredRandom (3), experimental (4), targeted (5), opportunistic (6) 1 sensor_method SensorMethod: activityDetection (1), timeLapse (2), both (3) 1 animal_types AnimalTypes: unmarked (1), marked (2), both (3) 1 bait_use BaitUse: none (1), scent (2), food (3), visual (4), acoustic (5), other (6) 1 event_interval seconds, 0 or more 0 keywords list of strings; a keyword can hold spaces and commas, but not a double quote empty abstract, methods, description free text, up to 2000 characters each none

The four choice fields have an enumeration in trapper_client. Its members are the integers Trapper stores and carry the label it shows, so an editor can autocomplete them. The field accepts the member, its number or its label, and anything else is rejected with the list of valid values:

BaitUse.SCENT            # <BaitUse.SCENT: 2>
BaitUse.SCENT.label      # "scent"
ResearchProjectCreate(name="N", acronym="ABC", bait_use="scent")    # same as BaitUse.SCENT or 2

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
The creator becomes the project's administrator. members adds the other users that join it, each with a role:

from trapper_client import ResearchProjectCreate, ResearchProjectMember, ResearchProjectRoleType

ana = next(iter(client.users.where(search="ana")))

project = client.research_projects.create(
    ResearchProjectCreate(
        name="Doñana mammals",
        acronym="DONMAM",
        members=[
            ResearchProjectMember(user=ana, role=ResearchProjectRoleType.EXPERT),
            ResearchProjectMember(user=7, role="collaborator"),
        ],
    )
)
print([(r.username, r.roles) for r in project.project_roles])
# [('ana', ['Expert']), ('rp_staff', ['Admin']), ('user7', ['Collaborator'])]
  • user is the User that client.users returns, or its primary key.
  • role is a ResearchProjectRoleType (ADMIN, EXPERT or COLLABORATOR), its number or its label, in any case.
  • A user cannot appear twice (the model refuses it), and the account that creates the project cannot be listed: it is already the administrator. Both fail before anything is sent. A user that does not exist is rejected by Trapper, naming the row (project_roles-1-user: Select a valid choice.).
  • The members can only be given when the project is created: changing the roles of an existing project is a web action the SDK does not cover.

docs.title: What it returns
docs.text:
• A staff account: the project is active at once and create() returns it.
  • Any other account: Trapper creates the project but keeps it not approved, and hides it from the API until an administrator approves it. create() then returns None: the project exists, it just cannot be read back yet.

docs.title: When the server rejects the form
docs.text:
A name or acronym already in use, or an acronym of the wrong length, makes Trapper re-render the form (status 200). create() raises APIError naming the field:

Research project creation failed (status 200): name: Research project with this Name already exists.

Pass raise_on_error=False to get None instead. What the model can check locally (empty name, acronym length, an unknown choice, ...) raises ValidationError before anything is sent.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — same code on both. See Trapper versions.

client.resources — individual media files (images/videos) recorded at a deployment.

Endpoints:

  • GET /storage/api/resources (list + detail)
  • GET /storage/api/resources/collection/{collection_pk} (scoped to a collection)
  • GET /storage/api/resources/location/{location_pk} (scoped to a location)

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description pk comma-separated PKs Filter by specific resource PKs resource_type choice Filter by resource type status choice Filter by resource status rdate_from, rdate_to date date_recorded range udate_from, udate_to date date_uploaded range rtime_from, rtime_to HH:MM Time-of-day range on date_recorded owner boolean true = only resources owned/managed by current user locations_map list of PKs Filter via deployment__location (v1 only: Trapper v2 ignores it) collections list of PKs Filter by one or more collection PKs (any of them) deployments list of PKs Filter by deployment PKs (any of them) tags list of PKs Filter by tag PKs observation_type string Full-text search for observation_type:<value> species list of PKs Full-text search for species_id:<value> timestamp_error boolean true = resources outside the deployment's date range search string Full-text search across name and data vectors

Lists (pk, locations_map, collections, deployments, tags, species) can be given as a list or as a comma-separated string: collections=[2, 3] and collections="2,3" are the same. Trapper reads each one in a different form (deployments and collections as repeated parameters, pk and locations_map as one string with commas), and gets it wrong without telling you when given the other: deployments="1,2" is ignored and returns every resource, collections="2,3" is a 400, pk=[1, 2] keeps one pk and locations_map=[1, 2] finds nothing. The SDK sends each one the way Trapper reads it.

A filter that Trapper does not apply

Trapper ignores a parameter that is not one of its filters without an error, and the list comes back unfiltered; the SDK emits an UnknownFilterWarning that names it (the request is still sent). Besides those in the table, the list applies name, deployment, mime_type, file_size, token and file_checksum_hash. locations_map is ignored by v2, and ordering and in_bbox by both. deployment__isnull, which an older version of this guide listed, makes Trapper answer 500 on v1 and v2, whatever the value: the SDK warns about it and there is no filter for the resources without a deployment. To silence the warning: warnings.simplefilter("ignore", err.UnknownFilterWarning).

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
# Lazy iteration with filters (all() is the same thing)
for res in client.resources.where(status="Public", deployments=12):
    print(res)

# One page
page = client.resources.get(page=1, page_size=100, resource_type="I")

# Single item
item = client.resources.find(123)

# CSV export
client.resources.export(file="resources.csv", status="Public")

See Usage if any of this looks unfamiliar — it's the same interface on every component.

docs.title: Dates
docs.text: date_recorded is a timezone-aware datetime (2024-03-10T20:49:43+01:00 in Trapper's JSON), so resources can be compared and sorted by when they were taken. One that cannot be read stays as the text it came as, and an empty one is None. export(file="x.csv") writes it back as ISO text.

docs.title: Downloading the file
docs.text:
The REST API lists resources but does not serve their files: url and url_original are paths of a classic web view (/storage/resource/media/<pk>/file/) that does not accept the API token. With a token, or with no login, it answers 404, and it does so both when the file does not exist and when the account may not see it. download() logs in with user_name and user_password (the account's email on servers that log in by email), like the imports do, and saves the file:

client = TrapperClient(base_url=..., access_token=..., user_name="me@example.org", user_password="...")

path = client.resources.download(29, "images/")                          # a directory: saved as 29-original.jpg
path = client.resources.download(29, "photo.jpg")                        # or a file name
thumb = client.resources.download(29, "thumb.jpg", kind="thumbnail")     # "original", "preview" or "thumbnail"

for res in client.resources.where_by_collection(5):
    client.resources.download(res.pk, "collection-5/")
  • The file is streamed to disk, into a temporary .part file that is moved into place when it is complete, so a failure never leaves a half-written file.
  • Network failures and 502/503/504 answers are retried with exponential backoff (tenacity): retry_attempts (3, the first try included; 1 disables it), retry_min_wait and retry_max_wait. A download that was cut is started again from the beginning. A 404 and any other answer are not retried.
  • A 404 raises NotFoundError saying it can be the file or the permission. A preview or a thumbnail may not exist if Trapper did not generate them.
  • download() raises ValueError if the client has no user_name/user_password.
  • A Trapper that is not behind the proxy that serves its files (a development server on its own port) answers 200 with an empty body and an X-Accel-Redirect header; download() raises APIError saying so instead of saving an empty file. Checked on Trapper v2 (the original JPEG); on v1 only against such a server.

Not a stable API contract

It depends on an unversioned web view, like the imports.

docs.title: Downloading all the files of a deployment or a collection
docs.text:
Trapper has no endpoint for it: it is download() once per resource. deployments.download_resources() and collections.download_resources() do that loop, and need user_name and user_password like download():

report = client.deployments.download_resources(12, "downloads/")          # downloads/<deployment_id>/<name>.jpg
report = client.collections.download_resources(5, "downloads/")           # downloads/<collection name>/<name>.jpg
print(report)        # 40 downloaded, 0 already there, 0 failed, in downloads/don01-2024a
  • Choosing which resources. Any filter of the resource list goes through, so the server does the choosing (resource_type="I", rdate_from/rdate_to, rtime_from/rtime_to, tags, species, search, pk=[...], and deployments=[...] for a collection), and filter_fn does it on the client for what the server cannot filter: client.deployments.download_resources(12, "out/", rdate_from="2024-03-01", filter_fn=lambda r: r.date_recorded.hour < 6). The first argument is called deployment_pk / collection_pk because pk is one of those filters.
  • A run can be repeated. A file that is already in the folder is skipped (skip_existing=True), and a file is only given its name when it is complete (it is a .part until then), so after an interruption or a failure you run the same call again and it carries on.
  • A failure does not stop the rest (on_error="continue"): it goes in report.failed ({resource pk: message}). on_error="raise" stops at the first one. Each file is retried like download() does (retry_attempts, ...).
  • The report (DownloadReport): downloaded, skipped (lists of paths), failed, ok and total.
  • Names. <name><extension>, the extension from the resource's mime; -<pk> is added when two resources share a name; a file name is cleaned of characters a file system refuses. kind="thumbnail" or "preview" saves <name>-thumbnail.jpg, next to the originals. The folder of a collection is flat: the resource list does not say which deployment a resource belongs to.
  • Progress. progress_callback(event, data) is called for every file with "downloaded", "skipped" or "failed" and {"resource", "path", "index", "total"} ("error" too for a failure); total is None with a filter_fn.
  • It works over the list of resources you give it, too: client.resources.download_many(resources, "folder/").

docs.title: Scoped to a collection or a location
docs.text:
Every access pattern has a _by_collection/_by_location counterpart, hitting /storage/api/resources/collection/{collection_pk} or /storage/api/resources/location/{location_pk} instead of the unscoped endpoint:

# All resources by collection (lazy)
for res in client.resources.where_by_collection(collection_pk=5):
    print(res)

page = client.resources.get_by_collection(collection_pk=5, page=2, page_size=25)
result = client.resources.get_all_by_collection(collection_pk=5)
res = client.resources.find_by_collection(collection_pk=5, resource_pk=123)

# All resources by location (lazy)
for res in client.resources.where_by_location(location_pk=42):
    print(res)

page = client.resources.get_by_location(location_pk=42, page_size=10)
result = client.resources.get_all_by_location(location_pk=42)
res = client.resources.find_by_location(location_pk=42, resource_pk=99)

This is also how you list resources within a collection — CollectionsComponent itself only lists collections, not the resources inside one.

docs.title: Sequences
docs.text:
Trapper compatibility

v1 ✔ · v2 ✔ — same code on both. See Trapper versions.

client.sequences — resource sequences: events grouping resources recorded within a configurable time interval of each other.

Endpoint: GET /media_classification/api/sequences (list + detail). This endpoint is not paginated server-side — get_all()/where()/all() still work transparently, since the single unpaginated response is treated as page 1 of 1.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description sequence_id int Filter by sequence id sequence_uuid str Filter by sequence UUID interval int Filter by grouping interval (seconds) collection PK Filter by classification-project-collection PK deployment comma-separated PKs Filter by deployment PKs of member resources

docs.title: The six access patterns
docs.text:
This component has no special methods — it's exactly the generic interface described in Usage:

page = client.sequences.get(page=1, page_size=50)
for seq in client.sequences.where(collection=35):
    print(seq)
result = client.sequences.get_all()
seq = client.sequences.find(1)
client.sequences.export(file="sequences.csv")
